## Installation

### Option 1: CLI Install (Recommended)

Use [npx skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) to install skills directly:

```bash
# Install all skills
npx skills add coreyhaines31/marketingskills

# Install specific skills
npx skills add coreyhaines31/marketingskills --skill cro copywriting

# List available skills
npx skills add coreyhaines31/marketingskills --list
```

The CLI detects which agents you have installed and asks where to install. For Claude Code it installs into `.claude/skills/`; universal agents share `.agents/skills/`.

> [!TIP]
> If you run the command from **inside** an agent session (e.g., asking Claude Code to install the skills for you), the CLI runs non-interactively and may only install to the universal `.agents/skills/` directory, which Claude Code does not read. Pass the agent explicitly:
>
> ```bash
> npx skills add coreyhaines31/marketingskills -a claude-code
> ```

### Option 2: Claude Code Plugin

Install via Claude Code's built-in plugin system:

```bash
# Add the marketplace
/plugin marketplace add coreyhaines31/marketingskills

# Install all marketing skills
/plugin install marketing-skills
```

> **Note:** `/plugin` is only available in an interactive Claude Code CLI session. It is **not** available in Claude Code on the web, GitHub Actions, or other non-interactive/remote environments — in those cases you'll see `/plugin isn't available in this environment`. Use **Option 1 (`npx skills`)** instead, or the equivalent CLI commands:
>
> ```bash
> claude plugin marketplace add coreyhaines31/marketingskills
> claude plugin install marketing-skills@marketingskills
> ```

### Option 3: OpenAI Codex Plugin

Install via Codex's plugin system:

```bash
# Add the marketplace
codex plugin marketplace add coreyhaines31/marketingskills

# Then browse and install from inside a Codex session
/plugins
```

Select **marketing-skills** to install all skills. To pick up new releases later, run `codex plugin marketplace upgrade`.

### Option 4: Clone and Copy

Clone the entire repo and copy the skills folder:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills.git
cp -r marketingskills/skills/* .agents/skills/
```

### Option 5: Git Submodule

Add as a submodule for easy updates:

```bash
git submodule add https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills.git .agents/marketingskills
```

Then reference skills from `.agents/marketingskills/skills/`.

### Option 6: Fork and Customize

1. Fork this repository
2. Customize skills for your specific needs
3. Clone your fork into your projects

### Option 7: SkillKit (Multi-Agent)

Use [SkillKit](https://github.com/rohitg00/skillkit) to install skills across multiple AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc.):

```bash
# Install all skills
npx skillkit install coreyhaines31/marketingskills

# Install specific skills
npx skillkit install coreyhaines31/marketingskills --skill cro copywriting

# List available skills
npx skillkit install coreyhaines31/marketingskills --list
```

### Option 8: Claude Web Skill ZIPs

Download the desired `<name>-claude-web.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills/releases/latest), then use **Customize → Skills → + Create skill → Upload a skill** in Claude. Each archive contains one skill. Account permissions and code execution must allow skills.

The web-target archive uses an explicitly reviewed shorter description; its instructions and resources are preserved. The attached web manifest lists any skills whose description still needs review; newly created release notes also summarize omissions. Installing a ZIP does not configure local CLIs, MCP servers, credentials, or related skills. See [release packaging and verification](docs/skill-release-packaging.md) for archive contents, source variants, and unverified client limitations.

### Option 9: Perplexity Computer Skill ZIPs

Download the desired `<name>-perplexity.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills/releases/latest), then in Perplexity Computer use **Plugins → Add custom → Skill → Upload skill**. These archives keep the original skill files with `SKILL.md` at the root, which Perplexity requires; the source and Claude web ZIPs nest the skill in a folder and won't upload there. Installing a ZIP doesn't configure local CLIs, MCP servers, or related skills.

## Upgrading from v1.x to v2.0

v2.0 renames 17 skills and consolidates `page-cro` + `form-cro` into a single `cro` skill. If you installed the v1.x skills, you'll have **stale old-name folders** in your install directory after upgrading — the new skills install alongside the old ones, so you'll see both `skills/page-cro/` and `skills/cro/`, etc. Clean them up:

```bash
# From the directory where you installed the skills (e.g., .agents/skills/ or .claude/skills/)
rm -rf page-cro form-cro \
       ab-test-setup analytics-tracking aso-audit competitor-alternatives \
       email-sequence free-tool-strategy launch-strategy onboarding-cro \
       paid-ads paywall-upgrade-cro popup-cro pricing-strategy \
       product-marketing-context referral-program schema-markup \
       signup-flow-cro social-content
```

Then reinstall the v2.0 skills via your usual method (e.g., `npx skills add coreyhaines31/marketingskills`).

### Migrate the product marketing context file

In v2.0 the context file moved from `.claude/` to `.agents/` and was renamed from `product-marketing-context.md` to `product-marketing.md`. Move your existing context file:

```bash
mkdir -p .agents
# v2.0 file (or pre-v2.0 file with new name)
mv .claude/product-marketing.md .agents/product-marketing.md 2>/dev/null
# pre-v2.0 file with legacy name
mv .claude/product-marketing-context.md .agents/product-marketing.md 2>/dev/null
```

Skills will still check `.claude/` and the legacy `product-marketing-context.md` filename as fallbacks, so nothing breaks if you don't migrate.

### Full rename map

| Old | New |
|-----|-----|
| `ab-test-setup` | `ab-testing` |
| `analytics-tracking` | `analytics` |
| `aso-audit` | `aso` |

| `paid-ads` | `ads` |
| `paywall-upgrade-cro` | `paywalls` |
| `popup-cro` | `popups` |
| `pricing-strategy` | `pricing` |
| `product-marketing-context` | `product-marketing` |
| `referral-program` | `referrals` |
| `schema-markup` | `schema` |
| `signup-flow-cro` | `signup` |
| `social-content` | `social` |

## Usage

Once installed, just ask your agent to help with marketing tasks:

```
"Help me optimize this landing page for conversions"
→ Uses cro skill

"Write homepage copy for my SaaS"
→ Uses copywriting skill

"Set up GA4 tracking for signups"
→ Uses analytics skill

"Create a 5-email welcome sequence"
→ Uses emails skill
```

You can also invoke skills directly:

```
/cro
/emails
/seo-audit
```

## Skill Categories

### Growth Engineering

### Sales & RevOps

repositories.name: LoopForge
repositories.description: Self-hosted workflows for coding-agent delivery. Orchestrate CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code with scripts and human approval gates. Includes Local workflows for coding assistants.
repositories.readme:
English · 简体中文

Two ways to work · Quick start · SOPs · Features · Local · FAQ · Docs

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8af401d9-1aae-427c-b4bc-455c12d17beb

80-second product tour (1080p, with sound).

**LoopForge** is a self-hosted workspace where your team ships software with coding agents. Describe what you need to **Main Bot** in chat: it opens a Docker sandbox, checks out your repositories, delegates to project roles, and opens the PR. When a way of working proves itself, save it as an **SOP** (a standard workflow of agents, scripts and human gates) so the next requirement is delivered the same way, with review and approval built in. Coding-agent CLIs do the work: CodeBuddy, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Antigravity, Kimi Code, Pi, DeepSeek Harness and ZCode. LoopForge adds the roles, sandboxes, checkpoints and history around them, all on your own infrastructure under the MIT license. ## Two ways to work | | **Chat with Main Bot** | **Run an SOP** | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Exploring, quick fixes, iterating with the agent | Repeatable delivery with fixed stages and sign-off | | How it runs | Main Bot opens a [conversation workspace](docs/conversation-workspaces.md) (a Docker sandbox with your repos) on demand and calls project roles as subagents | The engine runs Agent, Script, Human-gate and sub-SOP nodes in order, in their own sandbox | | You stay in control by | Queuing or steering messages mid-reply, and pausing, resuming or taking over a running SOP from chat | Approving at human gates, sending work back to a chosen step, retrying or rerunning from any node | | Delivers | A PR/MR, or a direct merge into a shared branch (`mode=direct`) | Documents, code or a PR, plus per-node artifacts and logs | Both paths track the same **requirements**, so every change, whether made in chat or by an SOP, links back to what was asked for and counts toward delivery and cost reports.

The chat home. Type a request, @ a role, skill, requirement, SOP or repository, and pick the executor, model and permission mode per conversation.

## Why LoopForge Ask a coding agent to "fix this bug" and the result depends on that run. It might skip the plan, forget the tests, review its own code, or stop halfway without anyone noticing. That's fine for a demo, but it isn't how a team ships. - **Repeatable.** Same SOP, same stages, same checks for every requirement. Start from built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs. - **Separated roles.** Planning, implementation, review and testing each get their own prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools. A role works as an SOP node or as a subagent in chat. - **Human in the loop.** Approval gates where they matter. Read the report, approve, or send the work back to a chosen step. - **Observable and resumable.** Node status, tool traces, logs and artifacts in one place. Pause, retry a failed step, or rerun from any node. - **Your stack, your servers.** Ten coding-agent CLIs as executors, from CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code to OpenCode, Cursor CLI and more. GitHub, Skills and MCP as tools. Docker sandboxes or your own machine as the runtime. ## Quick start Install **Git** and clone the repository first. The installer checks Docker, Compose, Python 3 and curl and offers to install missing components. Python/curl installation supports apt, dnf and yum on Linux; the Compose plugin supports x86_64/arm64 and verifies the official release SHA-256. macOS needs a working Python 3 and Docker Desktop; Homebrew can install missing components. Ordinary Linux users are supported through Docker group access or sudo. Set `LOOPFORGE_YES=1` to accept installation prompts. Package and image downloads require internet access. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Tencent/LoopForge.git cd LoopForge ./start.sh ``` `./start.sh` pulls the GHCR release image pinned in `compose.yaml` without building locally (`bash scripts/install.sh` does the same). It creates the MySQL and platform services, generates configuration and session secrets, and installs the built-in sandboxes, starter SOPs and welcome project. Host Go and Node.js installations are not required. Configure model API keys and GitHub authorization after startup. Use `./start.sh logs`, `stop`, `restart` or `pull` to manage it, and `./start.sh dev` to build the checkout from source. If downloads from `ghcr.io` stall, set `MIRROR` to a registry host that can stand in for `ghcr.io`. `./start.sh` pulls from that host and tags the image back to the name pinned in `compose.yaml`. Setting `MIRROR` trusts that host, because the download is tagged with the official name. The GitHub Release records the digest; `docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' ghcr.io/tencent/loopforge:` should show the same digest after `@`. Without `MIRROR`, `./start.sh` still pulls `ghcr.io` directly, and `compose.yaml` stays unchanged. Upgrade with the same variable and `./start.sh pull`. [ghcr.nju.edu.cn](https://doc.nju.edu.cn/books/e1654/page/ghcr) is one such host. A Docker `registry-mirrors` entry such as `https://docker.nju.edu.cn` only accelerates Docker Hub and is not a value for `MIRROR`. ```bash MIRROR=ghcr.nju.edu.cn ./start.sh ``` Open the address printed by the installer and create your account; the first one becomes the administrator. The service listens on `0.0.0.0:8090` by default. On a cloud host, the installer reads the public IP from the provider's metadata service and prints it; allow the port in your security group, or put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front. Restrict access to your own IP until the administrator account exists. The home page's quick-access guide walks you through adding a model key, connecting a repository and choosing an SOP. For GitLab, Gitea, Gogs and other Git hosts, [set up Git SSH](docs/deployment.md#git-repositories-over-ssh) to check out and push branches with a personal key. PR/MR and Issue automation requires a hosting API token or a separately configured MCP. ### Try it without an API key New accounts join the **LoopForge demo project**, which includes an SOP made only of a script and a human gate: 1. Switch to the demo project, open **Templates**, and open **Platform check · script & approval**. 2. Click **Run SOP**. A real script writes a report, then the run waits for you at the approval step. 3. Approve it from **Needs review** or the run page, and watch the run continue to its final artifact. ### What you need for real work | I want to… | You need | | --- | --- | | Run the script + approval demo | Nothing | | Chat with Main Bot, generate a document or a new project | An API key for the selected executor | | Change an existing repository (in chat or via an SOP) and open a PR | Model credentials and a GitHub repository (connect GitHub in personal settings) |
More setup details: executors, GitHub, sandboxes, access model
- **Executors.** Pick one of ten CLIs beside the home composer, then a model. Every SOP role can choose its executor independently (built-in roles default to CodeBuddy). Requirement clarification, AI notification summaries, Bot replies and run evals currently use CodeBuddy, so their model pickers list CodeBuddy models only and the server refuses a model of another CLI instead of switching it to CodeBuddy; scheduled assistant tasks run on the CLI the task selects. | Executor | Credentials | Installation | | --- | --- | --- | | **CodeBuddy** | Personal key, or a shared key an administrator configures for chat and SOP runs | In the Docker image | | **Codex** | Personal key; a connected execution machine can use its local login | In the Docker image | | **Claude Code** | Personal key; a connected execution machine can use its local login | Installed from npm on first use, then cached | | **OpenCode · Kimi Code · Pi** | Personal key only | Installed from npm on first use, then cached | | **DeepSeek Harness** | Personal key only | In the Docker image | | **Cursor CLI · Antigravity** | Personal key only | Provider installer on first chat use; not installed into SOP sandboxes | | **ZCode** | Personal key only | Not bundled; install it on the service or execution machine PATH | The seven agent CLIs after Claude Code keep their model and MCP configuration in a private home directory per run, so they always use the responsible user's own key and Base URL from personal settings, even on a connected execution machine. When rolling them out to a team, each member configures their own credentials. First-use installs need npm or provider access; [native deployments](docs/deployment.md#workers-and-runners) need the CLI for the executor you choose. - **GitHub is optional.** All built-in generic SOPs run without a repository: product SOPs deliver documents, and new frontend/backend projects deliver source files in the task workspace. Bug fixes still need source code and reproduction details. Connect a repository when you work on existing code or want PRs. - **Delivering to a repository.** Choose **Connect GitHub** in personal settings, approve the device code on GitHub and pick your repository (the LoopForge OAuth App is built in; no PAT required, manual PAT entry still works). Set executor credentials (or bind a local execution machine), then either run a project SOP or ask Main Bot to change the code and submit a PR/MR. - **Sandboxes.** In the default Compose installation, SOP runs and conversation workspaces both use Docker sandbox containers started through the host Docker socket. Default sandboxes reuse the installed runtime image, so nothing extra is built after installation; custom Dockerfiles still build their own images. Docker socket access grants control of the host daemon, so this setup is for trusted teams, not untrusted multi-tenant isolation. See [deployment boundaries](docs/deployment.md#accounts). Re-running the installer keeps your data. - **Accounts and access.** New installations listen on all interfaces (existing bind settings are kept) and are designed for a trusted team: signed-in users can read project data across the instance, and teammates can sign up from the login page (`AGENTFLOW_ALLOW_SIGNUP=false` in `.env` turns that off). Read the [account and access model](docs/deployment.md#accounts) before exposing it beyond your team. - **Remote access, HTTPS, separate workers.** See [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). - **Hacking on LoopForge itself?** `bash scripts/dev.sh` runs it natively (Go 1.26.11+).
## How SOPs work An **SOP** is the workflow a delivery follows. Agents, scripts and people take part in the same run:

The SOP designer with the built-in bug-fix SOP. Each step picks a role; failed checks can send the work back to an earlier step.

| Node | What it does | | --- | --- | | **Agent** | A role (prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools) that designs, implements, reviews or tests. | | **Script** | A deterministic shell step: build, test, lint, generate a report. No AI where AI is not needed. | | **Human gate** | Pauses the run until someone checks the artifacts and approves, or sends the work back to a step. | | **Sub-SOP** | Runs another SOP as a sub-workflow. | | **Preview build** | Builds a static site and archives it for review. | Each node declares its artifacts and dependencies, and the engine starts each step once its dependencies complete. Start from a built-in SOP, adapt its roles, rules and environment to your project, and publish versions as it evolves.

A run waiting at a human gate: approve and continue, add context and rerun the step, or send the work back upstream.

**A delivery we actually ran:** four CodeBuddy roles planned a Python fix, implemented it, reviewed it independently and summarized the delivery. Three real tests passed; the run waited for human approval, then verified the accepted code had not changed. The [reusable acceptance case](e2e/api/45-delivery-model.test.mjs) checks the files and results. See the [validation record](docs/validation.md) for scope and known gaps. ## Features | Area | What you get | | --- | --- | | **Chat workbench** | Main Bot with per-conversation executor, model and permission mode. `@` references for roles, skills, requirements, SOPs and repositories. Messages queue while a reply runs; *Steer* interrupts and sends now. Generated files open in a side panel with preview, source and download. | | **Conversation workspaces** | On-demand Docker sandboxes with the project's repositories checked out, project roles as native subagents, and direct control of a running SOP workspace: pause, resume or take over. | | **SOP designer** | Visual canvas with Agent, Script, Human gate, Sub-SOP and Preview nodes, rework-on-failure edges, validation, version history and publishing. Built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs. | | **Roles** | Reusable definitions: prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills, MCP tools, artifacts and gates, shared across SOP nodes and chat subagents. | | **Requirement → delivery** | Requirements tracked end to end, whether shipped by an SOP or straight from chat, with PR/MR status tracking, merge detection and direct-branch merges. | | **Runs & approvals** | Live node status, tool traces, worker logs, per-node artifact snapshots and workspace previews. A single **Needs review** inbox for every gate waiting on you. | | **AI scheduled tasks** | Recurring agent tasks with full workspace, SOP and MCP access; a shared market of versioned, parameterized task templates; automatic SOP dispatch for new requirements. | | **Insights & cost** | Engineering metrics, business-domain reports with static HTML/SVG export, and token/cost accounting for SOPs and conversations at public list prices. | | **Execution environments** | Platform workers, Docker sandboxes, or a connected local execution machine using your own tools and repositories. | | **Team-ready** | Password accounts, projects and members, light/dark/system themes, an OpenAPI-described HTTP and MCP API. Management pages are in English and Chinese; the chat workbench is Chinese for now. |

Built-in SOPs are read-only blueprints; copy one into your project to run and edit it.

## LoopForge Local Don't want to run a server? **LoopForge Local** brings the built-in delivery workflows straight into the coding assistant you already use: ```bash # Run inside your target project, e.g. for Claude Code npx -y loopforge-cli@latest install claude ``` Then run `/start-devflow ""` in Claude Code. | Host | Supported | | --- | --- | | Claude Code · CodeBuddy · Codex · Cursor | Classic (default) and Portable editions | | Pi | Portable edition | | DeepSeek Harness | Portable edition | | Hermes Agent | Portable edition | See the [local guide](docs/local/usage.md) for each host's entry point and [editions](docs/local/editions.md) for the differences. Source lives in [`local/`](local/). Local runs the built-in workflows today; exporting a platform SOP for standalone local execution is planned. | | Platform | Local | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Teams sharing chat workspaces, SOPs, approvals and history | One developer inside an IDE or CLI | | Needs | Docker + Python 3 | Node.js 20+, Python 3.8+ and a coding assistant | | Workflows | Chat with Main Bot + custom SOPs on a visual canvas | Built-in Classic / Portable workflows | | Evidence | Shared run details, approvals and metrics in the web workspace | Artifacts under `artifacts/{task_slug}/` + optional local dashboard | ## FAQ **Do I need an API key to try it?** No. The demo SOP uses only a script and a human gate. Chat and agent steps need a key for the executor you pick. Model usage is not included; you bring your own credentials. **Do I need GitHub?** No. Chat, documents and new projects run in the task workspace. Connect GitHub when you want to change an existing repository or open PRs. **Should I use chat or an SOP?** Use chat to explore and iterate; Main Bot can still open a PR. Once you find a way of working you want every requirement to follow, with fixed reviewers, tests and sign-off, put it in an SOP. Main Bot can start, pause and take over SOP runs, so the two paths work together. **How is this different from Dify, n8n or Flowise?** Those are general-purpose AI and automation workflow builders. LoopForge is built for **software delivery with coding agents**: implementer and reviewer roles, Docker sandboxes with real repositories, GitHub delivery, human acceptance gates and run evidence. **How is this different from using Claude Code, Codex, CodeBuddy or another coding CLI directly?** LoopForge doesn't replace them; it orchestrates them. Each agent step and each chat turn runs one of those CLIs. LoopForge adds what surrounds it: who does what, in which sandbox, in which order, with which checks, and who signs off. **Is it safe to expose on the internet?** New installations listen on all interfaces and target a trusted team. Read the [account and access model](docs/deployment.md#accounts) and set up HTTPS before opening it up. Report vulnerabilities privately via the [security policy](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation | I want to… | Start here | | --- | --- | | Deploy, manage accounts, connect execution machines | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | | Understand chat workspaces, scheduled AI tasks and token pricing | [Conversation workspaces](docs/conversation-workspaces.md) · [AI scheduled tasks](docs/ai-scheduled-task-capabilities.md) · [Token pricing](docs/token-pricing.md) | | Install local workflows or choose an edition | [LoopForge Local](docs/local/usage.md) · [Editions](docs/local/editions.md) | | Extend the platform or use the HTTP / MCP API | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [API reference](docs/api/README.md) · [Shared schedules API](docs/api/shared-schedules.md) | | Contribute to the UI | [Frontend design conventions](design.md) (Chinese) | | Check functional coverage and release readiness | [Validation record](docs/validation.md) · [Acceptance matrix](docs/testing/acceptance-matrix.md) · [Release review](docs/release-readiness.md) | | Understand source provenance and maintenance | [Public scope](docs/open-source-scope.md) · [Upstream synchronization](docs/upstream-sync.md) | ## Community Scan the QR code to join the LoopForge community group. ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome: share a use case, report a bug, or improve workflows, integrations and the platform experience. Start with the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). Security issues go through the [security policy](SECURITY.md). If LoopForge is useful to you, a star helps others find it. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party components keep their own licenses and notices; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

repositories.name: multica
repositories.description: Make humans and AI agents work as one team — open-source and self-hostable.
repositories.readme:
**Agents that show up on the board.** Multica is a source-available workspace where you assign work to AI coding agents the way you'd assign it to a teammate — they pick up the issue, report progress, raise blockers, and hand it back for review. Self-hostable, works with the agent CLIs you already use, no lock-in. [![CI](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/multica-ai/multica?style=flat)](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica/releases) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/multica-ai/multica?style=flat)](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica/stargazers) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/W8gYBn226t)

[Website](https://multica.ai) · [Docs](https://multica.ai/docs) · [Quickstart](https://multica.ai/docs/cloud-quickstart) · [Download](https://multica.ai/download) · [Vision](VISION.md) · [Self-Hosting](SELF_HOSTING.md) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/W8gYBn226t) · [X](https://x.com/MulticaAI) **English | [简体中文](README.zh.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md)**

Your next 10 hires won't be human.

--- ## What is Multica? You already run Claude Code, Codex, and three other agents. Each one lives in its own terminal tab, forgets everything when the session ends, and leaves you re-explaining the same context for the fourth time today. The more agents you add, the more of your day goes to babysitting them. Multica puts those agents and your teammates in one workspace. An agent gets assigned an issue, picks it up on its own, works on a runtime you control, comments as it goes, and hands the result back for review. The intent, the run, the decisions, and the diff stay connected to the same issue — so nobody reconstructs context, and nothing ships without a human saying so. --- ## Build the team. *Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi — you don't pick one. You hire them all.*

- **[The agent CLIs you already use](#runtimes) →** Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Kimi, OpenCode, and more. - **[Agents as teammates](https://multica.ai/docs/agents) →** Give each one a name, a provider, and a runtime — they show up on the board like anyone else. - **[Squads](https://multica.ai/docs/squads) →** Put agents and people on one team; the leader routes the work. - **[Skills](https://multica.ai/docs/skills) →** Turn a solved problem into a playbook every agent reuses. - **[Your own runtime](https://multica.ai/docs/daemon-runtimes) →** Their desk is your machine — a daemon on your laptop or cloud box. Code never leaves it. ## Hand off the work. *It starts as three rough sentences in an issue. It ends as a pull request.*

- **[Assign an issue](https://multica.ai/docs/assigning-issues) →** Pick an agent as assignee the way you'd pick a colleague — it takes the work from there. - **[Autopilots](https://multica.ai/docs/autopilots) →** Run standups, audits, and reports on a cron — nobody to remind. - **[Chat](https://multica.ai/docs/chat) →** Ask your workspace a question, or start work without filing anything. - **[Projects](https://multica.ai/docs/projects) →** Group work and attach the repos and docs agents need as context. ## Stay in the loop. *Which agent touched this? What did it run? What did it cost? Open the run.*

- **[Execution log](https://multica.ai/docs/tasks) →** Replay every tool call, command, and error, timestamped. - **Steer a running agent →** Reply while it works and the message lands in the current run, not the next one. Claude Code, Codex, Grok, and Kiro today. - **Usage analytics →** See what each run cost, per agent and per issue. - **[Review gates](https://multica.ai/docs/issues) →** Work lands in review, not in main. You decide what ships. - **[Inbox](https://multica.ai/docs/inbox) →** Get pinged when an agent needs a call, not for every step. - **[Retries and timeouts](https://multica.ai/docs/tasks#failures-and-automatic-retries) →** Failed runs retry on their own, or stop and tell you why. ## Make it yours. *Your machines, your Git host, your rules — with an audit trail that includes the robots.* - **[Self-host everything](SELF_HOSTING.md) →** Docker Compose or Helm, on your own infrastructure. - **[Your Git host](https://multica.ai/docs/vcs-integration) →** GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, or Forgejo — self-hosted included. - **[Workspaces](https://multica.ai/docs/workspaces) →** Separate agents, issues, and settings per team. - **[Roles](https://multica.ai/docs/members-roles) and [access scopes](https://multica.ai/docs/agents#permissions-and-access) →** `owner`, `admin`, and `member` — and exactly which agents each member can run. - **[Security model](https://multica.ai/docs/security-model) →** What an agent can reach, and what it can't. - **[Slack, Feishu/Lark, DingTalk, WeCom, and Telegram](https://multica.ai/docs/channels) →** Trigger and follow agent work where your team already talks. New Feishu/Lark connections are open to mainland-China Feishu only for now; DingTalk, WeCom, and Telegram are [community-maintained](https://multica.ai/docs/community-maintained). - **Web, [desktop](https://multica.ai/docs/desktop-app), and [mobile](https://multica.ai/docs/mobile-app) →** The same workspace on macOS, Windows, Linux, iPhone, and iPad — the iOS app builds from source today, not yet on the App Store. - **[CLI and API](https://multica.ai/docs/cli) →** Every surface is scriptable. Agents drive Multica through the same CLI you do. --- ## Get started - **Cloud** — sign up at **[multica.ai](https://multica.ai)**. No terminal required. - **Desktop** — download **[Multica Desktop](https://multica.ai/download)** for macOS, Windows, or Linux. It connects the computer it runs on as a runtime automatically. - **Self-host** — run the whole stack on your own infrastructure; see below. The one prerequisite: the machine that will run agents needs at least one [supported agent CLI](#runtimes) installed and signed in — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and friends. Multica drives them; it doesn't ship them.
Self-hosting the whole thing
```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/multica-ai/multica/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --with-server multica setup self-host ``` On Windows, set `$env:MULTICA_MODE="with-server"`, then run the PowerShell installer: `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/multica-ai/multica/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex`. This pulls the official images from GHCR and requires Docker. See the [Self-Hosting Guide](SELF_HOSTING.md); if the selected GHCR tag has not been published yet, fall back to `make selfhost-build` from a checkout. A self-hosted server sends one anonymous, deployment-level snapshot a day: the release version plus bucketed counts, with no names, content, or IDs. Set `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` on the API server to turn it off — [what's collected](SELF_HOSTING.md#anonymous-deployment-telemetry).
### Your first agent in five minutes **1. Connect a computer.** A *runtime* is any machine agents can work on — your laptop, or a cloud box. Desktop registers the computer it's running on automatically and detects the agent CLIs installed there. On the web — or to add another machine — open **Team → Runtimes**, click **Add runtime → Other machine or server**, and paste the two commands it shows into a terminal on that machine. **2. Create an agent.** Open **Team** in the sidebar and click **+** (**New agent**). Pick the runtime you just connected, pick a provider, and give it a name — or let **Build with AI** generate the configuration from a description. That name is how it shows up on the board and in comments. **3. Assign it something.** File an issue and set the agent as assignee. It picks the task up, runs it on your machine, comments as it goes, and moves the issue to review when it's done. Full walkthrough: [Quickstart](https://multica.ai/docs/cloud-quickstart) · [Tutorial](https://multica.ai/docs/tutorial) --- ## Runtimes Multica does not ship a model. It drives the agent CLIs you already have installed and authenticated — the current source supports 31 — so switching providers is a dropdown, not a migration. | Provider | CLI | Provider | CLI | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code | `claude` | OpenAI Codex | `codex` | | Cursor Agent | `cursor-agent` | GitHub Copilot CLI | `copilot` | | OpenCode | `opencode` | OpenClaw | `openclaw` | | Hermes | `hermes` | Pi | `pi` | | Antigravity | `agy` | CodeBuddy | `codebuddy` | | DevEco Code | `deveco` | Grok | `grok` | | Kimi | `kimi` | Kiro CLI | `kiro-cli` | | Qoder CLI | `qodercli` | Qoder CN | `qoderclicn` | | Qwen Code | `qwen` | QwenPaw | `qwenpaw` | | Reasonix | `reasonix` | Trae CLI | `traecli` | | DeepSeek Harness | `dsh` | Oh-My-Pi | `omp` | | MiniMax Code | `mcode` | Dim | `dim` | | Huawei Cloud CodeArts | `codearts` | ZeroClaw | `zeroclaw` | | Muse Code | `muse` | Devin CLI | `devin` | | Amp | `amp` | Factory Droid | `droid` | | ZCode | `zcode` / ZCode Desktop | | | Installing and authenticating them: [Install an agent runtime](https://multica.ai/docs/install-agent-runtime) · [Providers](https://multica.ai/docs/providers) --- ## Documentation | I want to… | Start here | | --- | --- | | Get an agent doing something today | [Quickstart](https://multica.ai/docs/cloud-quickstart) · [Tutorial](https://multica.ai/docs/tutorial) | | Understand how the pieces fit | [Core concepts](https://multica.ai/docs/concepts) · [How Multica works](https://multica.ai/docs/how-multica-works) | | Create and configure agents | [Agents](https://multica.ai/docs/agents) · [Create an agent](https://multica.ai/docs/agents-create) · [Skills](https://multica.ai/docs/skills) | | Get work to an agent | [Triggering agents](https://multica.ai/docs/triggering-agents) · [Assigning issues](https://multica.ai/docs/assigning-issues) · [Mentions](https://multica.ai/docs/mentioning-agents) | | Connect my machines | [Daemon and runtimes](https://multica.ai/docs/daemon-runtimes) · [Install an agent runtime](https://multica.ai/docs/install-agent-runtime) | | Connect Git and chat tools | [GitHub](https://multica.ai/docs/github-integration) · [Self-hosted Git](https://multica.ai/docs/vcs-integration) · [Channels](https://multica.ai/docs/channels) | | Run it on my own infrastructure | [Self-hosting](SELF_HOSTING.md) · [Security model](https://multica.ai/docs/security-model) · [Environment variables](https://multica.ai/docs/environment-variables) | | Script it | [CLI reference](https://multica.ai/docs/cli) · [CLI and daemon guide](CLI_AND_DAEMON.md) · [Auth tokens](https://multica.ai/docs/auth-tokens) | | Drive Multica from Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor | [Multica CLI skill](https://github.com/multica-ai/multica-cli) | | Work out why an agent is stuck | [Runs](https://multica.ai/docs/tasks) · [Troubleshooting](https://multica.ai/docs/troubleshooting) | The docs are also available in [简体中文](https://multica.ai/docs/zh), [日本語](https://multica.ai/docs/ja), [한국어](https://multica.ai/docs/ko), and [Français](https://multica.ai/docs/fr). --- ## Architecture ``` Web (browser) Desktop (Electron) iPhone · iPad (Expo) │ │ │ ▼ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ │ │ │ Next.js │ │ │ │ pages + API │ │ │ │ proxy │ │ │ └──────┬───────┘ │ HTTPS + WebSocket │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐ │ Go backend (Chi + WebSocket) │──>│ PostgreSQL 17 │ └─────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘ └───────────────┘ │ runs over WebSocket ┌───────┴────────┐ │ Agent daemon │ runs on your machine, next to your code └───────┬────────┘ │ spawns ┌─────────────────┴──────────────────┐ │ Claude Code · Codex · Cursor · … │ └────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` | Layer | Stack | | --- | --- | | Web | Next.js 16 (App Router) | | Desktop | Electron, sharing the web UI packages | | Mobile | Expo / React Native (iPhone and iPad) | | Backend | Go (Chi router, sqlc, gorilla/websocket) | | Database | PostgreSQL 17 (`pgcrypto` + `pg_trgm`) | | Agent runtime | Local daemon executing any [supported agent CLI](#runtimes) | --- ## Development Contributors: start with the [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). **Prerequisites:** [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 22, [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/) 10.28.2, [Go](https://go.dev/) 1.26.9, [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) ```bash make dev ``` `make dev` auto-detects your environment (main checkout or worktree), creates the env file, installs dependencies, sets up the database, runs migrations, and starts every service. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full workflow, worktree support, testing, and troubleshooting. The iOS client lives in [`apps/mobile/`](apps/mobile/) — its [README](apps/mobile/README.md) covers building it onto your own device. We release most weekdays, so `main` moves quickly — pull often. --- ## Why "Multica"? **Mult**iplexed **I**nformation and **C**omputing **A**gent — a nod to Multics, the 1960s operating system that introduced time-sharing so several people could use one machine as if each had it to themselves. Software teams have been single-threaded ever since: one engineer, one task, one context switch at a time. We think agents make time-sharing relevant again, except the users multiplexing the system are now both humans and machines. A small team shouldn't feel small. The longer argument, and where we think this goes: **[VISION.md](VISION.md)**. --- ## License [Multica License](LICENSE) — the complete Apache License 2.0 text plus additional conditions covering hosted services, commercial embedding, and branding. Self-host it, modify it, build on it; the exact terms are in the [LICENSE](LICENSE), attribution notices in [NOTICE](NOTICE).

repositories.name: omnigraph
repositories.description: Object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology
repositories.readme:
Object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology.
Unified retrieval engine (vector/BM25/graph) · Git-style workflows · Open data format (Lance)

Quickstart  ·  Docs  ·  Cookbooks  ·  CLI  ·  Studio  ·  llms.txt

Omnigraph is engineered for the new workload introduced by long-horizon agents: multiple agents sharing a typed world model to continuously retrieve and update context and coordinate work. Agents and UIs can become thin stateless consumers of durable state. Omnigraph Cloud is in private preview: [join the waitlist](https://www.omnigraph.dev/cloud?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=cloud-waitlist). Join the [Omnigraph Slack community](https://join.slack.com/t/omnigraphworkspace/shared_invite/zt-3wfpglyxj-lHvJGhuySPfqLtN35uJZNw) to ask questions, share feedback, and follow development. ## Capabilities | Capability | What it gives you | |---|---| | **Typed ontology** | Agents share one enforceable model of the domain. `.pg` schemas declare node and edge types, keys and constraints, and the engine enforces them on every write. | | **Multimodal retrieval** | Agents assemble high-precision & recall context in one query: graph traversal + vector ANN + full-text + Reciprocal Rank Fusion in **one** runtime, with filtering. | | **Branching** | Agents propose reviewable changes instead of writing to main: a branch per agent or task, three-way merge, time travel across the whole graph. | | **Declared as code** | A `cluster.yaml` declares graphs, schemas, stored queries, embedding providers and policies. `cluster plan` previews, `cluster apply` converges, Terraform-style. | | **Security as code** | Cedar policy enforced **server-side on every mutation**, per graph or server-wide; bearer auth, server-resolved actors, audit tracking. | | **Object-storage native, open format** | Decoupled storage and compute. Store graphs on local disk or S3-compatible storage: RustFS / MinIO, AWS S3 / R2, or Azure preview. Graph data uses open, versioned [Lance](https://github.com/lance-format/lance), including Blob values. | ## What you can build | Use case | What it's for | |---|---| | **Company brain** | Org knowledge unified into one graph every agent can query | | **Agentic memory** | Durable, versioned memory: a branch per agent or per task, merged on review | | **Context graph** | Decision traces and codified tribal knowledge for retrieval | | **Dev graph** | Issues & dependency model that coding agents read and write | | **R&D / ML data layer** | Experiments and trials written into branches, versioned for training & eval | ## Install ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph/main/scripts/install.sh | bash ``` This installs `omnigraph` (CLI) and `omnigraph-server` into `~/.local/bin` from published release binaries. Or with Homebrew: ```bash brew tap ModernRelay/tap brew install ModernRelay/tap/omnigraph ``` ## Studio [Omnigraph Studio](https://www.omnigraph.dev/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=studio) is the desktop app for your graphs. Browse each type as a table, follow relationships on a canvas, write queries with the compiler's errors as you type, and review what a branch changes before you merge it. It is a native Rust app on GPUI, the framework behind Zed, for macOS, Windows and Linux. Open a graph on one of your server targets in Studio: ```bash omnigraph studio --target --graph ``` [Download Studio](https://www.omnigraph.dev/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=studio) or read [its source](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-studio). ## Set it up with an AI agent Omnigraph is built to be run by coding agents. Two ways in: **Teach your agent the playbook.** The `omnigraph` binary carries the [**`omnigraph` agent skill**](skills/omnigraph) written for it: the operational playbook covering cluster mode, the two config surfaces, schema evolution, query linting, data writes, branches, Cedar policy, and the common gotchas. Export it where your agent loads skills, so the skill always matches the installed CLI: ```bash omnigraph skill export ~/.claude/skills/omnigraph --force ``` With an older CLI that has no `skill` command, or none installed, `npx skills add ModernRelay/omnigraph@omnigraph` installs the copy on the default branch instead. **Or have an agent set it up from scratch.** Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, or any agent that can read a URL and run a shell command: ```text Read https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph/blob/main/skills/omnigraph/references/onboarding.md and follow it to set up Omnigraph for me. ``` The agent installs the CLI, asks what the graph is for, builds and queries a small local graph, and then points to the cookbooks, a cluster or Omnigraph Cloud. For ready-to-run graphs with real seed data (company brain, VC operating system, pharma & industry intel), [`ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks`](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks) is the fastest way to see Omnigraph shaped to a real domain. ## Deploy A **cluster** declares graphs, schemas, stored queries, and policies in a configuration bundle. `cluster plan` previews changes and `cluster apply` submits them to the selected destination. The cluster-only HTTP server exposes graphs at `/graphs/{id}/…` and activates applied changes without a restart. Keep desired configuration separate from its destination: ``` company-brain/ ├── cluster.yaml ├── people.pg # schema for the "knowledge" graph ├── queries/ # stored queries: the .gq files ARE the declaration │ └── people.gq ├── cluster.policy.yaml # deployment permissions └── graph.policy.yaml # graph permissions ``` ```yaml # cluster.yaml version: 1 metadata: name: company-brain graphs: knowledge: schema: people.pg queries: queries/ # every `query ` in queries/*.gq registers policies: cluster-access: file: cluster.policy.yaml applies_to: [cluster] graph-access: file: graph.policy.yaml applies_to: [knowledge] ``` For first boot, follow the [cluster guide](docs/user/clusters/index.md#bootstrap-a-cluster), including writer ownership transfer and authentication. The [deployment guide](docs/user/deployment.md) covers containers and object stores; Azure writers require its admission wrapper. The applied cluster policy must grant the authenticated operator `config_manage`. Schema changes also require `read` and `schema_apply` on the affected graphs. With those grants and a server target named `production`, deploy local edits: ```bash omnigraph cluster validate --config ./company-brain omnigraph cluster plan --target production --config ./company-brain omnigraph cluster apply --target production --config ./company-brain ``` `--config` names the source bundle; `--target` names the destination. Omitting `storage` from the bundle uses the selected destination's root. If present, `storage` must match that root; it never selects or redirects the target. Apply prints a deployment ID. If delivery is interrupted, inspect that ID before submitting again; see [deployment recovery](docs/user/clusters/index.md). ## Query and mutate Define a server target with `default_graph` and set `defaults.target` once in `~/.omnigraph/config.yaml` ([configuration](docs/user/cli/index.md)), and the everyday commands stay short. Stored queries and mutations run **by name**: ```bash omnigraph query search_docs --params '{"q":"AI safety"}' omnigraph mutate add_person --params '{"name":"Mina"}' ``` Branch, review and merge across the whole graph, so agents write in isolation: ```bash omnigraph branch create --from main agent/ingest-42 omnigraph branch merge agent/ingest-42 --into main ``` An **alias** is shorter still: bind a target, graph, and stored query to one name, then `omnigraph alias triage` runs it. Data commands use `--target NAME` for a configured server or managed resource, plus `--graph ID` when needed. Use `--target ./graph.omni` for a standalone local graph. Control-plane login and organization operations use `--profile`; see [operator configuration](docs/user/cli/targets.md). ## Security & governance - **Engine-wide enforcement:** every write path goes through the same Cedar gate, so the HTTP server, the CLI, and the embedded SDK obey identical rules. - **Declared in the cluster:** a policy bundle is bound to graphs (or the whole server) via `policies:` → `applies_to`. - **Scoped:** rules apply per graph, per branch, or server-wide. - **Static server credentials:** static bearer tokens are hashed at startup and compared in constant time. - **Forge-proof identity:** the actor is resolved server-side from the token; clients can't set it. See the [policy guide](docs/user/operations/policy.md). ## Clients & SDKs | Client | Use it for | Where | |---|---|---| | **TypeScript SDK** | typed access from Node / TS | [`@modernrelay/omnigraph`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@modernrelay/omnigraph) · [source](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-ts) | | **Built-in MCP** | connect an agent to the server's `/mcp`, directly or through `omnigraph mcp --target NAME` | [MCP guide](docs/user/operations/mcp.md) | | **Omnigraph Studio** | browse, query and review a graph in a desktop app | [download](https://www.omnigraph.dev/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=studio) · [source](https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-studio) | | **HTTP / OpenAPI** | use the wire contract from any language | [HTTP guide](docs/user/operations/server.md) · [OpenAPI](openapi.json) | Match the client's HTTP contract to the server's. The 0.14 server requires contract `0.14`; see [client availability](docs/user/install.md#client-compatibility) before selecting an npm package. ## Docs - [0.14 highlights and upgrade actions](docs/releases/v0.14.0-overview.md) · [User guide](docs/user/index.md) - [Cluster guide](docs/user/clusters/index.md) · [Deployment guide](docs/user/deployment.md) · [CLI reference](docs/user/cli/reference.md) - [Schema](docs/user/schema/index.md) · [Queries](docs/user/queries/index.md) · [Search](docs/user/search/index.md) · [Policy](docs/user/operations/policy.md) ## Build and test ```bash cargo build --workspace --locked cargo test --workspace --exclude omnigraph-gqt --exclude omnigraph-gqt-served --exclude omnigraph-dst --locked \ --features omnigraph-engine/failpoints,omnigraph-cluster/failpoints ``` Notes: - Rust stable toolchain, edition 2024 - The GQT corpus (`cargo test -p omnigraph-gqt`) and the DST suite (`cargo test` from `crates/omnigraph-dst`, which supplies its process environment) run separately; a plain `cargo test --workspace` starts the DST binaries without that environment and they refuse. Commands and CI gates: [docs/dev/testing.md](docs/dev/testing.md) - Full CI and some local test flows require `protobuf-compiler` - S3 integration tests expect an S3-compatible endpoint such as RustFS ## Contributing Please open an issue before sending large code changes — a maintainer triages it, and the `accepted` label is the green light for a PR (see [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md)). Concrete problem statements are the fastest way to collaborate on the roadmap. ## Community Join the [Omnigraph Slack community](https://join.slack.com/t/omnigraphworkspace/shared_invite/zt-3wfpglyxj-lHvJGhuySPfqLtN35uJZNw) to ask questions, share feedback, and follow development.
