repositories.name: openwhispr
repositories.description: Voice-to-text dictation app with local (Nvidia Parakeet/Whisper) and cloud models (BYOK). Privacy-first and available cross-platform.
repositories.readme:
OpenWhispr

The open-source and free alternative to WisprFlow and Granola.
Privacy-first voice-to-text dictation with AI agents, meeting transcription, and notes. Cross-platform for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Website · Docs · Download · API · Changelog

--- OpenWhispr turns your voice into text, notes, and actions from your desktop. Press a hotkey, speak, and your words appear at your cursor. Choose between fully private offline transcription with local speech-to-text models like Orukeet, Whisper, NVIDIA Parakeet, and Cohere Transcribe — where your audio never leaves your device — or cloud processing for speed. No data collection, no telemetry, fully open source. ## Download | Platform | Download | | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | [`.dmg`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | | macOS (Intel) \* | [`.dmg`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | | Windows | [`.exe`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | | Linux | [`.AppImage`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) / [`.deb`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) / [`.rpm`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) / [`.tar.gz`](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/releases/latest) | \* On Intel Macs, live speaker identification and voice fingerprinting are unavailable: they depend on ONNX Runtime, which [stopped shipping macOS x86_64 binaries in 1.24](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/tag/v1.24.1). Meetings still record and transcribe normally, and notes search falls back to keyword matching instead of semantic search. On macOS or x86_64 Linux, you can also install the community-maintained [Homebrew cask](https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/openwhispr): ```bash brew install --cask openwhispr ``` ## Features - **Voice dictation** — global hotkey to dictate into any app with automatic pasting - **Dictation translation** — dedicated hotkey to dictate in one language and paste the text in another - **AI agent** — talk to GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, Groq, Tinfoil, OpenRouter, or local models with a named voice assistant - **Voice Assistant hotkey** — dedicated hotkey that sends what you say straight to your AI assistant as a command, no wake word needed and no cleanup pass; highlighted text is edited in place. With auto-paste enabled, answers paste at a focused text cursor or stream into a floating panel and copy to the clipboard when no writable cursor is available. You can also opt in to sending a screenshot of your current screen as context - **Meeting transcription** — auto-detect Zoom, Teams, and FaceTime calls with live speaker diarization, voice fingerprinting, and Google, Microsoft, or Apple Calendar integration - **Local speaker diarization** — on-device speaker labelling with voice fingerprint recognition across meetings, no cloud required - **Notes** — create, organize, and search notes with folders, semantic search, cloud sync, and AI actions - **Team spaces & sharing** — free for signed-in users; share notes on the web with link, domain, or invite-only visibility, and collaborate in team spaces with roles, invitations, and server-enforced membership - **Audio import** — transcribe existing audio and video: drag in files, batch-upload, or paste a YouTube/audio URL, with optional speaker detection - **Local or cloud — your choice** — all core features (transcription, AI reasoning, speaker diarization, semantic search) work with local models or cloud providers — including GPU-accelerated local Whisper on Metal, CUDA, and Vulkan (AMD/Intel) - **Enterprise controls** — enforce organization policy, company SSO and SCIM, and centrally managed Amazon Bedrock or Azure OpenAI access without distributing cloud keys - **Public API & MCP** — manage notes and transcriptions programmatically or connect your AI assistant via the [MCP server](https://docs.openwhispr.com/integrations/mcp) ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr.git cd openwhispr npm install npm run dev ``` Requires Node.js 24+. See the [full documentation](https://docs.openwhispr.com/quickstart) for setup guides, platform-specific instructions, and build details. The commands above run the desktop application, which remains at the repository root. The Expo mobile application lives in [`openwhispr-mobile`](openwhispr-mobile/) with its own dependencies, lockfile, build configuration, and release process. See the [mobile README](openwhispr-mobile/README.md) for its setup instructions. ## Documentation Visit **[docs.openwhispr.com](https://docs.openwhispr.com)** for: - [Getting started](https://docs.openwhispr.com/quickstart) - [Platform guides](https://docs.openwhispr.com/platform/macos) (macOS, Windows, Linux) - [API reference](https://docs.openwhispr.com/api/overview) - [MCP server setup](https://docs.openwhispr.com/integrations/mcp) - [Troubleshooting](https://docs.openwhispr.com/troubleshooting) Repo examples: - [Custom ASR shim](examples/custom-asr-shim/) for Self-Hosted transcription against non-OpenAI-compatible ASR APIs ## Tech stack React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Electron 41, better-sqlite3, whisper.cpp, sherpa-onnx, shadcn/ui ## Star History [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=OpenWhispr/openwhispr&type=date&legend=top-left)](https://www.star-history.com/#OpenWhispr/openwhispr&type=date&legend=top-left) ## Sponsors

Neon is the serverless Postgres platform powering OpenWhispr Cloud.

## Contributing We welcome contributions. Fork the repo, create a feature branch, and open a pull request. See the [contributing guide](https://docs.openwhispr.com/contributing) for development setup and guidelines. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) — free for personal and commercial use. ## Acknowledgments - **[OpenAI Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper)** — speech recognition model powering local and cloud transcription - **[whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp)** — high-performance C++ implementation for local processing - **[NVIDIA Parakeet](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3)** — fast multilingual ASR model - **[sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx)** — cross-platform ONNX runtime for Parakeet inference - **[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/)** — model hub hosting Whisper, Parakeet, and embedding model weights - **[llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp)** — local LLM inference for AI text processing - **[Electron](https://www.electronjs.org/)** — cross-platform desktop framework - **[React](https://react.dev/)** — UI component library - **[shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/)** — accessible components built on Radix primitives - **[Neon](https://console.neon.tech/app/?promo=openwhispr)** — serverless Postgres powering OpenWhispr Cloud

repositories.name: context-mode
repositories.description: Free, local plugin that keeps tool output out of your coding agent's context window. Sandbox and SQLite FTS5 search, 99% fewer bytes in context. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and 4 more agents. Zero telemetry.
repositories.readme:
# Context Mode **A free, local plugin for 10 coding agents. It keeps tool output out of your agent's context window and keeps all usage data on your machine. The plugin is free forever.** [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/context-mode?label=npm%20downloads)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/context-mode) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/mksglu/context-mode?style=flat&color=yellow)](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1478479412700909750?label=Discord&logo=discord&color=5865f2)](https://discord.gg/DCN9jUgN5v) [![License: ELv2](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-ELv2-blue.svg)](LICENSE) **33K GitHub stars · 683K npm downloads** (read 2026-11-01, [stats.json](stats.json)) · on the Hacker News front page and GitHub Trending: [charts and sources](#adoption-stars-and-npm-downloads) > The Context Mode plugin is free and local, with its source open on GitHub. **Context Mode Gateway** is a separate hosted service with its own account and subscription. It takes the same idea from tool output to the whole conversation: Gateway Recall keeps long sessions searchable, and Gateway Memory shares what your agents learn across sessions and tools. [See how the Gateway works](https://contextmode.ai/docs/how-saving-works?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=quote) **Contents:** [Why](#why) · [Adoption](#adoption-stars-and-npm-downloads) · [Install](#install) · [Try it](#try-it) · [Use cases](#use-cases) · [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Tools](#tools) · [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) · [Context Mode Gateway](#context-mode-gateway) · [License](#license) · [Community](#community) ## Why A coding agent reads files, runs commands and fetches pages, and every result goes into its context window. The Context Mode plugin runs that work in a local sandbox, keeps the full output in a SQLite index on your machine, and gives the agent the part it asks for. - **The plugin is free forever.** Use it at home and at work, free of charge, under a source-available license. - **Runs on your machine.** The hooks, the sandbox and search run as local processes next to your agent. - **The plugin keeps your data on your machine.** Every index lives in `~/.context-mode`: one `context.db` per project. - **Zero telemetry.** The plugin keeps all usage data on your machine. [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) lists each network call it makes. - **Works offline after install.** Sandbox runs, file indexing and search use local SQLite and your own runtimes. - **Thinking in Code.** The agent writes a short script instead of reading the data, and only what the script prints reaches the context: see [How it works, step 5](#thinking-in-code). - **Small replies.** On the 36 bench rows with 10 KB or more of raw output, the plugin's median reply is 99.4% smaller than the raw output. ## Adoption: stars and npm downloads
Open the [interactive chart](https://contextmode.ai/open-source/stats?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=adoption#daily) and point at a bar to read its value. Tabs there show days, weeks, months and years. Stars come from the GitHub GraphQL API (`starredAt`); npm downloads come from `api.npmjs.org/downloads/range`. The total up to 2026-10-29 is 683K npm downloads (`stats.json` keeps a daily copy). A daily job redraws both charts. - **Hacker News.** "MCP server that reduces Claude Code context consumption by 98%" reached the front page with 570+ points and 107 comments on 2026-02-28 ([thread](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47193064)). - **GitHub Trending.** A bot that watches GitHub Trending logged the repo there on 14 days from 2026-04-24 to 2026-10-17 ([uibm/trending-watcher](https://github.com/uibm/trending-watcher/issues?q=%22mksglu%2Fcontext-mode%22)). The agent reads files, runs the suite and fetches docs, and each result goes into the context window. When the window is full, the host compacts it, and from then on the agent sees a short summary plus your next message. Context Mode keeps the full output of each large tool call in `context.db` on your machine and gives the agent a small reply. At compaction, a snapshot of at most 2,048 B keeps the session state. After the compaction, the agent calls `ctx_resume` to read that snapshot back and `ctx_search` to find any earlier output by keyword. In the bench, a scripted session of 40 tool outputs and one compaction made a 442,893 B transcript, and the `ctx_resume` block that brought the agent back was 2,019 B (row `e-long-session` in the bench file; [open the case](bench/e-continuity/README.md#e-long-session)). In the same bench, one large log of 666,796 B put 3,380 B into the context, and the full log stayed in the index for `ctx_search` (row `d-synth-1m`; [open the case](bench/d-externalize/README.md#d-synth-1m)). How the snapshot picks what to keep: the [Long sessions guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/long-sessions?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=longer-sessions) and [ADR-0009](docs/architecture/adr/0009-compaction-and-memory.md). ### Speed Median of 5 runs, bench of 2026-11-01. | Measure | Result | |---|---| | Hook time over a bare `node` start, per agent | 7.5 ms to 12.3 ms | | `ctx_search`, 20 queries over 8 indexed files | 1.62 ms median, 6.70 ms max | | `ctx_index`, 3 real files, 625,649 B | 150 ms per MB | Source: rows `g-hook-kiro` to `g-hook-claude-code`, `g-search-latency` and `g-index-per-mb` of [the bench file](bench/results/2026-11-01-darwin-arm64.md), with every agent and query. Next, what happens inside one tool call, in [How it works](#how-it-works). ## How it works One tool call, in time order, from the install to a hook error. 1. **Install.** Each agent's own install command adds the MCP server, the hooks and the skills `ctx-doctor`, `ctx-stats` and `ctx-upgrade` to that agent's config folder, for example `~/.codex/skills//SKILL.md`. `context-mode setup` writes or repairs any part the native command leaves out ([ADR-0023](docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0023-native-install.md)). 2. **Session start.** The `SessionStart` hook opens the project database. When the session ran before, the agent gets one line that tells it to call `ctx_resume` ([dispatch.ts](src/core/hooks/dispatch.ts)). 3. **PreToolUse checks.** Before a tool runs, the `PreToolUse` hook checks the call in a fixed order: the user's deny list, WebFetch, curl and wget, inline HTTP and build commands, then a full-file Read over `OUTPUT_CAP` (16,384 B) and one-file shell dumps such as `cat` or `tail`. A Read with a line range runs as usual ([decide.ts](src/core/policy/decide.ts)). 4. **The exact call.** When a check matches, the hook stops the call and its reply names the exact `ctx_*` call to use, for example `ctx_execute` with `{"language":"shell","code":"","intent":""}`. For WebFetch the reply names `ctx_index`, then `ctx_search` ([read-deny.ts](src/core/policy/read-deny.ts)). 5. **The sandbox.** This is the Thinking in Code step: the agent's script runs here, and only what it prints comes back. `ctx_execute` writes the script to a temp folder and spawns the runtime from an argument list in the project folder. The timeout is `EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS` (600,000 ms, default and maximum); on timeout it stops the whole process group (`taskkill /F /T` on Windows). The child gets your environment minus preload variables such as `NODE_OPTIONS`, and the agent gets what the script prints, at most `OUTPUT_CAP` ([execute.ts](src/core/tools/execute.ts)). **Thinking in Code.** The agent sends a short script as a tool parameter, the script reads the data in the sandbox, and only what it prints goes into the context. Two real calls, in the form the Claude Code terminal shows them: `ctx_execute` on 5,000 JSON records, from the Claude Code 2.1.312 stream of the Try-it run with Context Mode 2.0.0-next.26 ([04-api-json.json](bench/evidence/try-it-2026-11-02/04-api-json.json)). The data is 1,039,898 B; the agent gets 254 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_execute (MCP)(language: "javascript", c…jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/photos\"); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(\"HTTP \" + res.status); const photos = await res.json(); let longest = null; for (const p of photos) { if (!longest || p.title.length > longest.title.length) longest = p; } const withEst = photos.filter(p => p.title.includes(\"est\")).length; const ties = photos.filter(p => p.title.length === longest.title.length).map(p => p.id); console.log(JSON.stringify({ total: photos.length, longest…nd count of titles containing \"est\"") ⎿ exit 0 · 239 B { "total": 5000, "longest": { "id": 653, "title": "temporibus commodi et fugit doloremque re…rit exercitationem necessitatibus aut", "length": 86 }, "longestTieIds": [ 653 ], "titlesContainingEst": 892 } ``` `ctx_batch` on an install log and a long git log, one live MCP call to `release-out/server.mjs` of Context Mode 2.0.0-next.36 on 2026-11-03 ([2026-11-03-ctx-batch.json](bench/evidence/thinking-in-code/2026-11-03-ctx-batch.json)). The commands print 228,881 B; the agent gets 8,667 B, the parts that match its two queries, and the full output stays in the index. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_batch (MCP)(commands: ["cat npm-install… queries: ["cache miss","feat commit"]) ⎿ ## cache miss js.org/@esbuild%2fwin32-x64 282ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2flinux-s390x 79ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2fopenbsd-x64 101ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2fwin32-arm64 99ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2fdarwin-arm64 99ms (cache miss) … +95 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` 6. **Indexing.** The full output goes into the index in chunks of at most `MAX_CHUNK_BYTES` (4,096 B). A Markdown chunk stays inside one heading section, and a code block that fits stays whole. Each chunk goes into two SQLite FTS5 tables: a Porter-stemmed table for words and a trigram table for paths, names and parts of words ([fts.ts](src/core/store/fts.ts)). `ctx_index` on a copy of this repo's `docs/how-it-works.md`, one live MCP call to `release-out/server.mjs` of Context Mode 2.0.0-next.36 on 2026-11-03 ([calls.json](bench/evidence/terminal-calls-2026-11-03/calls.json)). The file is 11,577 B; the agent gets 64 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_index (MCP)(path: "how-it-works.md") ⎿ Indexed 1 source(s), 17 chunk(s) from s1. Label: how-it-works.md ``` 7. **Search.** `ctx_search` ranks each table with BM25 and joins the two lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion: a hit scores 1/(`RRF_K` + rank), with `RRF_K` = 60. Before it returns an empty list, it tries a spelling fix from the indexed words. Search covers this session, this worktree (the default) or the whole project, and each snippet is at most `SNIPPET_MAX_BYTES` (800 B) ([search.ts](src/core/tools/search.ts)). `ctx_search` on that index, in the same run, in a project that also holds an `AGENTS.md`. One search reads the index and every agent's memory files. The agent gets 1,268 B: one content hit and one memory hit, each with its source and heading. For memory shared across machines, agents and sessions, see [Context Mode Gateway Memory](https://contextmode.ai/docs/memory?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=search-memory). ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_search (MCP)(queries: ["compaction state block"]) ⎿ Query "compaction state block": how-it-works.md #14: ### Session continuity The hooks log each prompt, edit, command, tool error, i…e same rows always give the same bytes. memory AGENTS.md #0: # Agent rules … +10 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` 8. **Run, then replace.** On hosts that run the tool first, the `PostToolUse` hook checks the result. Output over `REPLACE_TRIGGER_BYTES` (4,096 B) goes into the index whole, and the agent gets the best-matching chunks and one `ctx_search` line for the rest ([dispatch.ts](src/core/hooks/dispatch.ts)). 9. **Journal and compaction.** The hooks log each prompt, edit, command, tool error and decision in a journal. After a compaction the agent gets a state block of at most `STATE_BUDGET` (2,048 B), and each long line becomes a `ctx_resume(seq)` pointer to the full row; one `ctx_resume` reply is at most `RESUME_CAP` (2,048 B). On the next prompt, a prompt-match block brings back the journal rows that match it by BM25 ([ADR-0009](docs/architecture/adr/0009-compaction-and-memory.md)). `ctx_resume` with empty parameters returns the state block, in the same run: 209 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_resume (MCP)() ⎿ indexed how-it-works.md source s1: how-it-works.md (11536 B) more: ctx_search(queries:[], scope:"session") ``` 10. **The database.** Each project has one `context.db` under `~/.context-mode`, in Node's built-in `node:sqlite`. The database runs in WAL mode and runs a PASSIVE checkpoint on close. A new database gets built under a temp name and moves into place in one atomic step, and the busy timeout is `DB_TIMEOUT_MS` (5,000 ms) ([db.ts](src/core/store/db.ts)). 11. **A hook error.** A hook always ends with exit 0. On any error it gives the host's allow reply and writes one log line to `~/.context-mode/hook-errors.log`, so your agent keeps working. A spawned hook has `HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` (5,000 ms) ([fallback.ts](src/core/hooks/fallback.ts)). Every number with its reason: [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md). The rules the hook follows: [ADR-0008](docs/architecture/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md). Next, the [Tools](#tools) the agent calls. ## Tools | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `ctx_execute` | Runs code or a shell command in a sandbox; returns what it prints | | `ctx_batch` | Runs many commands, indexes the output, and searches it in one call | | `ctx_index` | Indexes a file, a text or a URL into the project database | | `ctx_search` | Searches the local index; returns the matching parts | | `ctx_resume` | Returns the plugin's local state block (at most 2,048 B), or one full row by `seq` | | `ctx_stats` | Shows how much output stayed out of context | | `ctx_doctor` | Checks the install; each check prints PASS or a fix command | | `ctx_upgrade` | Installs, upgrades or uninstalls; replaces old contextmode entries | | `ctx_purge` | Deletes indexed data by session, source or project | Three more real calls, from the same live run of Context Mode 2.0.0-next.36 on 2026-11-03 ([calls.json](bench/evidence/terminal-calls-2026-11-03/calls.json)). `ctx_stats`: the agent gets 3,097 B, the first line is the summary. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_stats (MCP)() ⎿ ctx_stats: 82.5% kept out all-time, 82.5% this session. … +59 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` `ctx_doctor` after `context-mode setup --agents claude-code`: 862 B, one row per check. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_doctor (MCP)() ⎿ Environment: context-mode 2.0.0-next.36 (8facf27), agent claude-code 0 (client r20-live) Environment: darwin-arm64, Node v26.8.1, shell /bin/zsh | Check | Status | Detail | Fix | |---|---|---|---| | D1 version | PASS | 2.0.0-next.36 (8facf27): ahead of next on npm (2.0.0-next.34) | | | D2 node | PASS | ok | | … +11 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` `ctx_purge` deletes one source: 66 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_purge (MCP)(source: "how-it-works.md") ⎿ ctx_purge: deleted 18 rows (scope: source). This cannot be undone. ``` Full reference: [Tools](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=tools). Commands in the agent: `/ctx-stats` shows the `ctx_stats` result, `/ctx-doctor` runs `ctx_doctor` (send its report with a defect report), and `/ctx-upgrade` runs `ctx_upgrade`, then `ctx_doctor`. ## Security and privacy - The plugin keeps all its data on your machine, one database per project in `~/.context-mode`, and `ctx_purge` deletes it by session, source or project. Read the [Security guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/security?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=security). - The plugin has zero telemetry: usage data, events and crash reports stay on your machine. It uses the network for four calls, each one started by you or your agent: | Call | When | File | |---|---|---| | Fetch of a URL, for `ctx_index` | Your agent asks for a page. The fetch blocks private and link-local addresses, checks each address the host name points to, connects to the address it checked, and checks again at each redirect. | [fetch.ts](src/core/sandbox/fetch.ts) | | One read of the npm dist-tags, with `git ls-remote` of the release tags as the fallback | You run `context-mode doctor`, to check for a new version | [doctor-env.ts](src/core/ops/doctor-env.ts) | | `npm i -g context-mode`, or `gh issue create` | You run `context-mode upgrade`, or you press a key to send the debug report | [commands.ts](src/cli/commands.ts) | | Your agent's own install command, npm or git | You install or update | Your agent | - The guard test D-PRIVACY-NET-1 in [tests/0008-enforcement.test.mjs](tests/0008-enforcement.test.mjs) scans the source for HTTP clients, sockets, DNS lookups, git network calls and gh or npm spawns. It flags each new call site, so this table stays true. - Doctor and the debug report remove secrets by their structure before they print. Code from `ctx_execute` runs on your host as your user, with your files, your network and your environment except the preload variables, so keep your agent's own permission prompts on. Here "sandbox" means the output stays in the sandbox and out of the context. What the plugin stores, where, and how to delete it: [Privacy](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/privacy?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=privacy). ## Context Mode Gateway The plugin works on tool output, on your machine, and it is complete on its own. Context Mode Gateway is a separate hosted service with its own account and subscription. It works on every request, across all your agents. Its 11 features, the full list: Context Saving, Recall, Memory, Skills, Search, Session resume, Active Context, Instructions, Protect, Prompt caching, Live and Analytics. Add the Gateway when you want savings on every request, memory across sessions and agents, or cost reports for a team. For one project on one machine, the plugin covers the job. The two work together: [Gateway guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/gateway?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=gateway). Gateway Recall, Search and Session resume run on the Gateway server, across sessions and agents. The plugin's `ctx_search` and `ctx_resume` read the local `context.db` of one project. With the Gateway on, your requests pass through its server; the plugin keeps its own data on your machine. | Product | Runs | Scope | Billing | |---|---|---|---| | Context Mode plugin | On your machine | One project, local `context.db` | Free | | Context Mode Gateway | Hosted service | All sessions and agents | Subscription, separate from the plugin | Set up the Gateway with one command: ```sh npx @context-mode/cli ``` `npx @context-mode/cli` signs you in to your Gateway account, which has its own subscription, and writes one config change per agent. Apps: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Codex Desktop, T3 Code, OpenCode and Pi. The Gateway CLI needs Node 20.12 or later, from its npm engines field. **Live.** One session as it runs: money saved this session, bytes kept out per request, history kept and sent, and a feed of each request with its cost and saving. Click the image for the full video. Docs: [How saving works](https://contextmode.ai/docs/how-saving-works?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=live)

Overview. Your spend and what the Gateway saved, per day, in one view.
Docs: How saving works
Analytics. Where each saving comes from: hidden tools, archived old results, large outputs kept in the archive and trimmed context.
Docs: How saving works

Spend. Spend per day and per model, cost per request and the cache hit rate, to help you plan a budget.
Docs: Prompt caching
Memory. Facts and decisions carry across sessions and agents. The screen shows what Recall saved and how many searches found an answer.
Docs: Memory

Skills. Add a skill once and all your clients use it when it helps. Import skills from GitHub and see the installed ones.
Docs: Skills
Protect. Rules that check each shell command before it runs. Here, a rule that stops terraform destroy.
Docs: Protect
Numbers in these screens come from the author's own account over 30 days (Oct 3 - Nov 1, 2026), so read them as one account's usage. Click an image for the full size. Three prompts to try with the Gateway on. The line under each one names the feature it shows. ```text Move this project from Jest to Vitest. Convert every test file, fix the config, run the suite after each batch, and tell me what is left. ``` Memory keeps the plan and the file list across a long job. ```text Pick up where we stopped yesterday on the Jest to Vitest move. What is done, what is left, and which test was failing? ``` Recall brings back yesterday's work in a fresh session. ```text Which date library did we choose on Tuesday, and why did we reject the other two? ``` Search finds the answer in past sessions.
Gateway features, from contextmode.ai/docs Source: [contextmode.ai/docs](https://contextmode.ai/docs/how-saving-works?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=features): | Feature | What it does | What you get | Details | |---|---|---|---| | Context Saving | Folds old tool output, runs data work as code (Thinking in Code), trims tool schemas, places cache marks | A tool output over 2,048 B becomes a short pointer, with the full copy archived | Saves the most on sessions with many tool calls | | Recall | The model sees recent work and an index of older work; the agent searches the archive for the rest | Gateway, Claude Code, Opus 5.5, 200K window, 2026-10-04: mean cost per session $4.8627 to $3.0353 (-37.6% in dollars, `ab.json` below) | Cost measured in Claude Code on Claude Opus 5.5 | | Memory | Each fact keeps two times: when it was true and when the Gateway learned it | Claude Code and Codex on one account share one store, tested end to end | The memory block goes into the first request of a new session | | Skills | A skill catalog on the Gateway for your account; it loads the skill that matches your message | The matching skill loads on the message that needs it | Import skills from GitHub; a loaded skill joins the prompt in full | | Search | Searches the prompts, commands and tool output that passed through, in the console and as an agent tool | Find any past prompt, command or tool output, from the console or your agent | The console searches the first 4,000 characters of each tool result | | Session resume | One command rebuilds a conversation as a native Claude Code or Codex session | Continue a conversation in Claude Code or Codex | Restores the text, tool names and a summary; the command is valid for 15 minutes | | Active Context | Sets how much a thread carries before its oldest parts move to the archive: 200K, 500K or 1M tokens | Pick the window size per thread | An image older than the kept part becomes a short text note | | Instructions | One text of at most 4,096 characters that tells every agent how to answer you | Read from the provider cache after the first request | Sets how the agent writes to you | | Protect | A tool-call firewall: checks shell commands, file reads and writes, web fetches and tool-server calls by what they do | Each call checked before it runs | Reads the call itself, so keep your agent's sandbox on for script files and paths built at run time; opt-in | | Prompt caching | Keeps requests cache-friendly: cache marks on the fixed part of the prompt and a cache for fetched pages | Inside the measured costs above | Uses up to 4 cache marks, the provider's maximum | | Live and Analytics | Shows each request and what the Gateway saved, as it happens and over time | See each request and its saving, live and over time | Covers every request that passes through the Gateway |
Gateway only: its cost against Claude Code alone, Claude Opus 5.5, mean dollars per session at list price. The plugin numbers are in [Benchmarks](#benchmarks). - Six short tasks (2026-09-29): 24.5% fewer dollars pooled over 176 sessions (21% to 29% per task). [v3-opus55-short.json](https://contextmode.ai/benchmarks/data/v3-opus55-short.json?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=bench) - Long Claude Code session, 200K window (2026-10-03/04): mean cost per session $4.8627 to $3.0353 (-37.6% in dollars, mean of 3 pairs). [ab.json](https://contextmode.ai/benchmarks/recall/200k-r2/ab.json?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=bench) - We fixed the rules before each run: [contextmode.ai/docs/benchmarks](https://contextmode.ai/docs/benchmarks?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=bench). The Gateway routes to Anthropic and OpenAI. The Gateway sends your requests to its server on the way to the model. It keeps a searchable record of your sessions for Recall and Search, and masks secrets and e-mail addresses when it reads archived output back. Its privacy page is at [contextmode.ai/privacy](https://contextmode.ai/privacy?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=privacy). Keep your agent's own sandbox on next to Protect. ## License Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2, the `LICENSE` file), a source-available license. You may use, copy, change and share the code, and use it at work, free of charge. The license keeps three uses for the licensor: 1. Offering the software to others as a hosted or managed service that gives them a large part of its features. 2. Moving, changing, turning off or getting around the license key functions, or removing or hiding what the license key protects. 3. Changing, removing or hiding the licensor's license, copyright or other notices. We chose ELv2 so the source stays open to all and the hosted service stays with the project. ## Community Report a defect on [Discord](https://discord.gg/DCN9jUgN5v) with the full `/ctx-doctor` report, and send ideas there too. The maintainer writes every change; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) shows how an agent files an issue. **Videos.** [Better Stack on Context Mode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QUHrntlfPo4). Make your own video and share it on [Discord](https://discord.gg/DCN9jUgN5v); we add videos over 10K views here.

repositories.readme: # Uptime Kuma Uptime Kuma is an easy-to-use self-hosted monitoring tool. [![GitHub Sponsors](https://img.shields.io/github/sponsors/louislam?label=GitHub%20Sponsors)](https://github.com/sponsors/louislam) ## 🥔 Live Demo Try it! Demo Server (Location: Frankfurt - Germany): It is a temporary live demo, all data will be deleted after 10 minutes. Sponsored by [Uptime Kuma Sponsors](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma#%EF%B8%8F-sponsors). > [!WARNING] > Be careful - the top result in Google, uptimekuma.co, is not our official website, we don't control the website. I recommend following the installation guide in this GitHub repo. ## ⭐ Features - Monitoring uptime for HTTP(s) / TCP / HTTP(s) Keyword / HTTP(s) Json Query / Websocket / Ping / DNS Record / Push / Steam Game Server / Docker Containers - Fancy, Reactive, Fast UI/UX - Notifications via Telegram, Discord, Gotify, Slack, Pushover, Email (SMTP), and [90+ notification services, click here for the full list](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/tree/master/src/components/notifications) - 20-second intervals - [Multi Languages](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/tree/master/src/lang) - Multiple status pages - Map status pages to specific domains - Ping chart - Certificate info - Proxy support - 2FA support ## 🔧 How to Install ### 🐳 Docker Compose ```bash mkdir uptime-kuma cd uptime-kuma curl -o compose.yaml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/master/compose.yaml docker compose up -d ``` Uptime Kuma is now running on all network interfaces (e.g. http://localhost:3001 or http://your-ip:3001). > [!WARNING] > File Systems like **NFS** (Network File System) are **NOT** supported. Please map to a local directory or volume. ### 🐳 Docker Command ```bash docker run -d --restart=always -p 3001:3001 -v uptime-kuma:/app/data --name uptime-kuma louislam/uptime-kuma:2 ``` Uptime Kuma is now running on all network interfaces (e.g. http://localhost:3001 or http://your-ip:3001). If you want to limit exposure to localhost only: ```bash docker run ... -p 127.0.0.1:3001:3001 ... ``` ### 💪🏻 Non-Docker Requirements: - Platform - ✅ Major Linux distros such as Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and ArchLinux etc. - ✅ Windows 10 (x64), Windows Server 2012 R2 (x64) or higher - ❌ FreeBSD / OpenBSD / NetBSD - ❌ Replit / Heroku - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) >= 20.4 - [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads) - [pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/) - For running Uptime Kuma in the background ```bash git clone https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma.git cd uptime-kuma npm run setup # Option 1. Try it node server/server.js # (Recommended) Option 2. Run in the background using PM2 # Install PM2 if you don't have it: npm install pm2 -g && pm2 install pm2-logrotate # Start Server pm2 start server/server.js --name uptime-kuma ``` Uptime Kuma is now running on all network interfaces (e.g. http://localhost:3001 or http://your-ip:3001). More useful PM2 Commands ```bash # If you want to see the current console output pm2 monit # If you want to add it to startup pm2 startup && pm2 save ``` ### Advanced Installation If you need more options or need to browse via a reverse proxy, please read: ## 🆙 How to Update Please read: ## 🆕 What's Next? I will assign requests/issues to the next milestone. ## ❤️ Sponsors Thank you so much for supporting this project! ### Special Sponsors [](https://www.atlascloud.ai) Atlas Cloud (https://www.atlascloud.ai) is sponsoring this project USD 400 per month for using their AI models. [![Powered by Atlas Cloud](https://www.atlascloud.ai/oss-program/powered-by-atlas-cloud.svg)](https://www.atlascloud.ai/?ref=UZCYBN) ### Open Collective and GitHub Sponsors (The list will be cached by GitHub, it may take up 24 hours to be updated) ## 🖼 More Screenshots Light Mode: Status Page: Settings Page: Telegram Notification Sample: ## Motivation - I was looking for a self-hosted monitoring tool like "Uptime Robot", but it is hard to find a suitable one. One of the closest ones is statping. Unfortunately, it is not stable and no longer maintained. - Wanted to build a fancy UI. - Learn Vue 3 and vite.js. - Show the power of Bootstrap 5. - Try to use WebSocket with SPA instead of a REST API. - Deploy my first Docker image to Docker Hub. If you love this project, please consider giving it a ⭐. ## 🗣️ Discussion / Ask for Help ⚠️ For any general or technical questions, please don't send me an email, as I am unable to provide support in that manner. I will not respond if you ask questions there. I recommend using Google, GitHub Issues, or Uptime Kuma's subreddit for finding answers to your question. If you cannot find the information you need, feel free to ask: - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/issues) - [Subreddit (r/UptimeKuma)](https://www.reddit.com/r/UptimeKuma/) My Reddit account: [u/louislamlam](https://reddit.com/u/louislamlam) You can mention me if you ask a question on the subreddit. ## Contributions ### Create Pull Requests Pull requests are awesome. To keep reviews fast and effective, please make sure you’ve [read our pull request guidelines](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#can-i-create-a-pull-request-for-uptime-kuma). ### Test Pull Requests There are a lot of pull requests right now, but I don't have time to test them all. If you want to help, you can check this: ### Test Beta Version Check out the latest beta release here: ### Bug Reports / Feature Requests If you want to report a bug or request a new feature, feel free to open a [new issue](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/issues). ### Translations If you want to translate Uptime Kuma into your language, please visit [Weblate Readme](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/blob/master/src/lang/README.md). ### Spelling & Grammar Feel free to correct the grammar in the documentation or code. My mother language is not English and my grammar is not that great.

repositories.readme:
# xtool

Cross-platform Xcode replacement. Build and deploy iOS apps with SwiftPM on Linux, Windows, and macOS.

## Overview

xtool is a cross-platform (Linux/WSL/macOS) tool that replicates Xcode functionality with open standards.

✅ Build a SwiftPM package into an iOS app

✅ Sign and install iOS apps

✅ Interact with Apple Developer Services programmatically

## Getting Started

1. Follow the guide to install `xtool`
    - [Installation (Linux/Windows)](https://xtool.sh/documentation/xtooldocs/installation-linux)
    - [Installation (macOS)](https://xtool.sh/documentation/xtooldocs/installation-macos)
2. Create and run your first xtool-powered app by following the [tutorial](https://xtool.sh/tutorials/xtooldocs/first-app)!

## Examples

### Screenshot

![A screenshot of xtool being invoked from VSCode](Documentation/xtool.docc/Resources/Cover.png)

### Command line interface

```bash
$ xtool --help
OVERVIEW: Cross-platform Xcode replacement

USAGE: xtool <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  -h, --help              Show help information.

CONFIGURATION SUBCOMMANDS:
  setup                   Set up xtool for iOS development
  auth                    Manage Apple Developer Services authentication
  sdk                     Manage the Darwin Swift SDK

DEVELOPMENT SUBCOMMANDS:
  new                     Create a new xtool SwiftPM project
  dev                     Build and run an xtool SwiftPM project
  ds                      Interact with Apple Developer Services

DEVICE SUBCOMMANDS:
  devices                 List devices
  install                 Install an ipa file to your device
  uninstall               Uninstall an installed app
  launch                  Launch an installed app

  See 'xtool help <subcommand>' for detailed help.
```

### Library

You can consume xtool itself as a Swift Package, to enable your own app to interact with Apple Developer Services, iOS devices, and more. You can use this by adding `XKit` or `XToolSupport` as a SwiftPM dependency.

Note: while we aim to uphold semver semantics on the CLI interface (breaking change = major version bump), the Swift interface does not offer the same guarantees.

```swift
// package dependency:
.package(url: "https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool", .upToNextMinor(from: "1.2.0"))
// target dependency:
.product(name: "XKit", package: "xtool")
```

repositories.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
repositories.description: Chrome DevTools for coding agents
repositories.readme:
# Chrome DevTools for agents

[![npm chrome-devtools-mcp package](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/chrome-devtools-mcp.svg)](https://npmjs.org/package/chrome-devtools-mcp)

Chrome DevTools for agents (`chrome-devtools-mcp`) lets your coding agent (such as Antigravity, Claude, Cursor or Copilot)
control and inspect a live Chrome browser. It is available as a
Model-Context-Protocol (MCP) server and as a [CLI][cli]. Both give your AI
coding assistant access to the full power of Chrome DevTools for reliable
automation, in-depth debugging, and performance analysis.

[Tool reference][tool-reference] | [CLI][cli] | [Skills][skills] | [Changelog][changelog] | [Contributing][contributing] | [Troubleshooting][troubleshooting] | [Design Principles][design-principles]

## Key features

- **Get performance insights**: Uses [Chrome
  DevTools](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-frontend) to record
  traces and extract actionable performance insights.
- **Advanced browser debugging**: Analyze network requests, take screenshots and
  check browser console messages (with source-mapped stack traces).
- **Reliable automation**. Uses
  [puppeteer](https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer) to automate actions in
  Chrome and automatically wait for action results.

## Disclaimers

`chrome-devtools-mcp` exposes content of the browser instance to the MCP clients
allowing them to inspect, debug, and modify any data in the browser or DevTools.
Avoid sharing sensitive or personal information that you don't want to share with
MCP clients.

`chrome-devtools-mcp` officially supports Google Chrome and [Chrome for Testing](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing/) only.
Other Chromium-based browsers may work, but this is not guaranteed, and you may encounter unexpected behavior. Use at your own discretion.
We are committed to providing fixes and support for the latest version of [Extended Stable Chrome](https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule).

Performance tools may send trace URLs to the Google CrUX API to fetch real-user
experience data. This helps provide a holistic performance picture by
presenting field data alongside lab data. This data is collected by the [Chrome
User Experience Report (CrUX)](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/crux). To disable
this, run with the `--no-performance-crux` flag.

## **Usage statistics**

Google collects usage statistics (such as tool invocation success rates, latency, and environment information) to improve the reliability and performance of Chrome DevTools MCP.

Data collection is **enabled by default**. You can opt-out by passing the `--no-usage-statistics` flag when starting the server:

```json
"args": ["-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest", "--no-usage-statistics"]
```

Google handles this data in accordance with the [Google Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).

Google's collection of usage statistics for Chrome DevTools MCP is independent from the Chrome browser's usage statistics. Opting out of Chrome metrics does not automatically opt you out of this tool, and vice-versa.

Collection is disabled if `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_USAGE_STATISTICS` or `CI` env variables are set.

## Update checks

By default, the server periodically checks the npm registry for updates and logs a notification when a newer version is available.
You can disable these update checks by setting the `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_UPDATE_CHECKS` environment variable.

## Requirements

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) [LTS](https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-schedule) version.
- [Chrome](https://www.google.com/chrome/) current stable version or newer.
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/)

## Getting started

Add the following config to your MCP client:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "chrome-devtools": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest"]
    }
  }
}
```

> [!NOTE]
> Using `chrome-devtools-mcp@latest` ensures that your MCP client will always use the latest version of the Chrome DevTools MCP server.

### MCP Client configuration

For setup instructions specific to your editor or agent (e.g. Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code), please see our [Client Configurations Guide][client-configurations-guide].

### Your first prompt

Enter the following prompt in your MCP Client to check if everything is working:

```
Check the performance of https://developers.chrome.com
```

Your MCP client should open the browser and record a performance trace.

> [!NOTE]
> The MCP server will start the browser automatically once the MCP client uses a tool that requires a running browser instance. Connecting to the Chrome DevTools MCP server on its own will not automatically start the browser.

## CLI

The package also includes the `chrome-devtools` CLI. Use it to control the browser from your terminal without MCP:

```sh
npm i chrome-devtools-mcp@latest -g
chrome-devtools navigate_page 1 --url "https://developers.chrome.com"
chrome-devtools take_screenshot 1 --filePath screenshot.png
chrome-devtools stop
```

See the [CLI guide][cli] for all commands and options.

## Skills

The package includes [skills](./skills) that teach your agent how to use Chrome DevTools:

| Skill                                                     | Use it to                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| [`chrome-devtools`](./skills/chrome-devtools)             | Debug and automate pages with the MCP tools.    |
| [`chrome-devtools-cli`](./skills/chrome-devtools-cli)     | Run the CLI and write shell scripts with it.    |
| [`a11y-debugging`](./skills/a11y-debugging)               | Audit and fix accessibility issues.             |
| [`cookie-debugging`](./skills/cookie-debugging)           | Debug cookies, sessions, and authentication.    |
| [`debug-optimize-lcp`](./skills/debug-optimize-lcp)       | Debug and improve Largest Contentful Paint.     |
| [`memory-leak-debugging`](./skills/memory-leak-debugging) | Find and fix memory leaks.                      |
| [`troubleshooting`](./skills/troubleshooting)             | Fix connection problems between MCP and Chrome. |

### Install skills as a plugin

A plugin installs the MCP server and all skills, including the CLI skill:

- **Claude Code:** Run `/plugin marketplace add ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp`, then `/plugin install chrome-devtools-mcp@chrome-devtools-plugins`.
- **Copilot / VS Code:** Run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source** and enter `ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp`.
- **Gemini CLI:** Run `gemini extensions install --auto-update https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp`.

See the [Client Configurations Guide][client-configurations-guide] for more information.

### Install skills manually

If your agent does not support plugins, copy the skill folders into the skills directory of your agent. The npm package contains the skills:

```sh
npm i chrome-devtools-mcp@latest -g
# Example for Claude Code. Use the skills directory of your agent.
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
cp -R "$(npm root -g)/chrome-devtools-mcp/skills/chrome-devtools-cli" ~/.claude/skills/
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The `chrome-devtools-cli` skill requires the CLI. Install the package globally before you use the skill.

### Keep skills up to date

Skills describe the tools of a specific version. Update the skills each time you update the MCP server or the CLI. Outdated skills can tell your agent to use tools or parameters that changed.

- **Plugins:** Use the update command of the plugin manager of your agent. The Gemini CLI command above enables automatic updates with `--auto-update`.
- **Manual installs:** Update the package, then copy the skill folders again:

```sh
npm i chrome-devtools-mcp@latest -g
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
cp -R "$(npm root -g)/chrome-devtools-mcp/skills/chrome-devtools-cli" ~/.claude/skills/
```

## Tools

If you run into any issues, checkout our [troubleshooting guide][troubleshooting].
See the full [Tool Reference][tool-reference] for a complete list of all supported MCP capabilities.

## Configuration

Find the complete list of server parameters (e.g., `--headless`, `--isolated`, `--slim`) and how to configure WebSocket connections in the [Configuration Guide][configuration-guide].

For basic browser tasks only, the `--slim` flag exposes a reduced set of tools. See the [Slim tool reference][slim-tool-reference].

## Advanced Usage

For advanced features such as handling concurrent sessions, persistent user data directories, using a custom or non-standard browser path (`--executablePath`), connecting to a running Chrome instance instead of starting a new one, or debugging on Android, see our [Advanced Usage Guide][advanced-usage-guide].

## Integrating as a browser subagent

If you are developing agentic tooling and want to provide an integrated browser subagent as part of your product, we recommend building on top of Chrome DevTools for agents.

For a reference implementation, see the [Gemini CLI browser agent documentation](https://geminicli.com/docs/core/subagents/#browser-agent).

repositories.readme:
# MAKO - Frame Generation, Scaling, and Shaders on SteamOS/Linux


> **Independent project:** MAKO is not an official Lossless Scaling, Decky Loader, lsfg-vk, vkBasalt, or ReShade release. MAKO does not contain or distribute Lossless Scaling, `Lossless.dll`, or extracted proprietary model payloads. The optional Lossless Scaling frame generation model (LSFG) and LS1 scaling read selected resources at runtime from a lawful, user-supplied Lossless Scaling installation; MAKO FG, the open MAKO Scaler, and bundled shaders do not require it. MAKO does not alter the user's DLL file, and translated resources remain process-local. Users are responsible for complying with the terms applicable to their copy. See Third-party notices. ## Downloads

| Component | Recommended for | Releases | | --- | --- | --- | | **MAKO Decky** | Steam Deck, Steam Machine, and Decky Loader users (bundles MAKO Renderer) | Latest MAKO Decky release (ZIP under Assets) | | **MAKO Renderer** | Direct Vulkan-layer installation without Decky | Latest MAKO Renderer release (Linux archive under Assets) | | **MAKO FG** | Standalone frame-generation model that can be used outside MAKO | MAKO FG model and runtime on Hugging Face | Published Renderer packages currently target x86_64 Linux hosts and include layers for both 64-bit and 32-bit x86 game processes. Native AArch64/Armada packages are not included in this release. MAKO is developed and tested on AMD GPUs with Mesa's RADV driver, including the Steam Deck. NVIDIA and Intel GPUs are community-tested. Options that need AMD hardware say so in the configuration guide. ## Community Join the official MAKO Discord for discussion, testing, development, showcases, and live troubleshooting. GitHub remains the source of truth for bug reports and feature requests. > [!TIP] > **Want update alerts?** MAKO Decky and MAKO Renderer are published independently. At the top-right of the MAKO GitHub repository page, click **Watch** > **Custom**, select **Releases**, then click **Apply**. GitHub will notify you when a new release is published, subject to your GitHub notification settings. ## ✨ Feature Highlights




- **Per-game frame generation models:** MAKO FG by default, or the optional Lossless Scaling models from your licensed installation, with quality and performance controls. - **Reduced ghosting:** MAKO FG is designed to preserve static HUD elements and reduce ghosts on thin moving objects at 4× and above. Full-quality v2 with LSFG Quality can also reduce ghosting; supported AMD GPUs gain extra safeguards. Results vary by game. - **Spatial scaling:** The open MAKO Scaler by default, or optional LS1 Quality and LS1 Performance, used alone or alongside frame generation. - **Per-game shaders:** Live sharpening, anti-aliasing, colour, cinematic, and retro effects through bundled vkBasalt. - **Adaptive Frame Generation:** Target 30–240 FPS with a selectable 2x–5x generation ceiling. - **Display-aware pacing:** Adapts frame delivery to the presentation plan and Gamescope VRR state. - **Experimental HDR:** HDR support for Scaling, Frame Generation, and Shaders through Gamescope. - **64-bit and 32-bit x86 support:** Matching Vulkan layers for native and Flatpak games. - **Gamescope recovery:** Preserves real frames during presentation pressure and Steam-menu transitions. - **Automatic profiles:** Saves per-game renderer and compatibility settings, matched by Steam app ID or process. - **Launcher integration:** Per-game setup for Heroic, Lutris, and EmuDeck, including Steam shortcuts. - **Native Steam Remote Play:** Opt-in frame generation, scaling, and shaders on the receiving device, controlled from MAKO Decky or the Qt UI. ## What MAKO is MAKO (**Motion-Adaptive Kernel Orchestration**) brings frame generation, spatial scaling, and bundled shader effects to Linux gaming. **MAKO FG and MAKO Scaler are the defaults and, with Shaders, work without Lossless Scaling. Only the optional Lossless Scaling frame generation model and LS1 scaling require it.** Scaling can run alone or alongside Fixed or Adaptive Frame Generation. The project consists of two closely integrated components: - **MAKO Decky** is the Decky Loader component, providing per-game controls, installation, updates, Flatpak preparation, and game launch integration. - **MAKO Renderer** is the Vulkan layer that provides the graphics pipeline for frame generation and spatial scaling; its packages also include optional bundled shader effects. ## In-game considerations > [!TIP] > **Try the game's V-Sync setting both on and off.** Neither setting is universally best: the result depends on the game, its FPS cap, VRR, and the compositor. Keep whichever option feels smoother and more responsive for that game. Every game and display behaves differently, so compare one setting at a time. If Frame Generation, Scaling, or Shaders do not work, try the game's Fullscreen, Borderless Fullscreen, and Windowed modes; none is universally best. For Scaling, also try different in-game resolutions and check that **Live Status** shows **Input** smaller than **Display**. Changing display mode can change the resolution MAKO processes and its GPU cost. See the configuration guide for which controls apply live and which require a restart. ## Install and use 1. **Install Decky Loader (if you haven't already).** Switch to Desktop Mode and follow the official Decky Loader installation guide, then return to Game Mode. 2. **Optional: Lossless Scaling (skip this step if you only want MAKO FG, MAKO Scaler, and Shaders).** To use the Lossless Scaling frame generation model or LS1 scaling, install the **default public version** of Lossless Scaling through Steam. Beta branches are not validated; the default public branch is recommended. 3. Open the latest MAKO Decky release and download its ZIP under **Assets**. 4. In Decky's settings, enable **Developer Mode**, then select **Developer > Install Plugin from Zip**. 5. Open **MAKO Decky** and select **Install MAKO Renderer**. Installing the ZIP alone does not install its bundled Renderer. 6. For a native Steam or Proton game, add this under **Steam Properties > Launch Options**: ```text /home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run %command% ``` 7. Start the game normally. 8. Experiment with the settings to find what works best for each game. Try Fixed or Adaptive Frame Generation, scaling, and shader effects independently. > [!IMPORTANT] > If Decky does not show or reload **MAKO Decky** after installing a ZIP, uninstall it, install the ZIP again, and restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. Then open the plugin and repeat step 5. ### Optional graphics integrations Shaders use bundled vkBasalt; no separate installation is needed. MAKO Decky also offers host-installed MangoHud and a per-profile **Gamescope WSI** compatibility option, independent of Scaling. See optional graphics integrations for ordering and limits. ### How to configure MAKO with third-party launchers - [Heroic](plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md#heroic) - [Lutris](plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md#lutris) - [EmuDeck](plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md#emudeck) - [Other Flatpak apps](plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md#manually-added-flatpak-shortcuts) - [Other non-Steam games](plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md#other-non-steam-games) For a step-by-step guide that creates a shareable report on the Desktop, see Collect MAKO Decky Diagnostics. ### Updating MAKO Decky 1. Quit the games using MAKO. 2. Uninstall MAKO Decky, then install the newer ZIP through **Developer > Install Plugin from Zip**. 3. Restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. 4. Open MAKO Decky and select **Install MAKO Renderer**, or **Update** when MAKO offers it, to install the version bundled in the ZIP. This also refreshes every MAKO Flatpak runtime extension already installed. Valid profiles and Steam launch options are kept. Removing or reinstalling MAKO Decky leaves Renderer, launchers, and the Remote Play override in place. Older Decky versions may remove Renderer; step 4 restores it. Invalid or unreadable Renderer configurations reset to defaults. **The ZIP updates MAKO Decky.** Apply the offered update inside Decky for Renderer, MAKO FG, and installed Flatpak extensions, even when the version number is unchanged. To remove Renderer, use **Remove MAKO Renderer** in Decky or the desktop **Uninstall MAKO Renderer** entry, which remains available after Decky is removed. ## Use MAKO Renderer directly Decky is optional. Desktop Linux users can install MAKO Renderer directly: 1. **Optional: Lossless Scaling (skip this step if you only want MAKO FG, MAKO Scaler, and Shaders).** To use the Lossless Scaling frame generation model or LS1 scaling, install the **default public version** of Lossless Scaling through Steam. Beta branches are not validated; the default public branch is recommended. 2. Download and extract `MAKO-Renderer-v-linux.tar.xz` from the latest MAKO Renderer release, then run **Install MAKO Renderer**. The installer opens **MAKO Renderer Configuration** and shows the launch option. 3. Create or select a profile and choose Frame Generation, scaling, and/or shader effects. Add the executable manually under **Profile Matching > Matched Processes**, or start the game normally and use **Detect Running Game…**, then close it. Detection only identifies the executable; it does not activate MAKO in the running game. 4. Every standalone native Steam or Proton game must start through MAKO. Add the option shown by the configuration window under **Steam Properties > General > Launch Options**, then use Steam's **Play** button normally: ```text ~/.local/bin/mako-launch %command% ``` Set this once per game; Steam applies it on every launch. Use the complete option shown by the window when shaders are enabled. The window can be closed during play. For direct desktop commands, see [Renderer usage](engine/README.md#usage); for shader details, see [Optional graphics integrations](engine/docs/LAYER-CHAINING.md#standalone-mako-renderer-with-vkbasalt). 5. For Flatpak games, launchers, or emulators, follow the [standalone Flatpak guide](engine/docs/FLATPAK-GUIDE.md) to install the matching extension and prepare each app, then launch it normally. The Renderer configuration window does not prepare Flatpaks, and the host `mako-launch` command cannot replace sandbox setup. Run the installer again to update. See the MAKO Renderer guide for manual installation and removal. > [!IMPORTANT] > MAKO Decky and the standalone archive share one native Renderer. Installing either selects its version: the standalone installer warns before replacing Decky's version, while Decky adopts a valid standalone installation or offers its bundled update when payloads differ, including same-version model changes. **Uninstall MAKO Renderer** removes the shared native files but keeps MAKO Decky and profiles; removing MAKO Decky preserves the independent Renderer and its launchers. Shared Flatpak extensions remain installed. ## Documentation These guides describe the selected branch. For a published version, select its `plugin-vX.Y.Z` or `render-vX.Y.Z` tag on GitHub; a development branch may document features that are not in the latest download. - MAKO Decky configuration: panel controls, profiles, runtime boundaries, and compatibility. - MAKO Renderer configuration: Qt controls, profiles, and game launch setup. - MAKO Renderer: direct installation, usage, builds, and architecture guides. - Troubleshooting and diagnostics: activation, presentation problems, and private reports. - Testing and releases: contributor validation and publication. - Ongoing maintenance: dependencies, version owners, upstream review triggers, and required checks. ## Featured in Community creators and publications have covered and tested MAKO on Steam Deck, Steam Machine, and Linux. See Featured In for videos, articles, and creator coverage. ## Credits and project lineage MAKO builds on and integrates work from these open-source projects and their communities: - **Kurt Himebauch / xXJSONDeruloXx** created the original Decky LSFG-VK plugin that formed the foundation of MAKO's Decky interface, installation workflow, and per-game controls. - **PancakeTAS** and the **lsfg-vk contributors** created the GPL-3.0-or-later version 2 Vulkan layer and Linux integration from which MAKO Renderer descends. MAKO's direct upstream baseline is 8b0da266; the exact lineage and migration commits are recorded in LICENSE.md. - **Georg Lehmann / DadSchoorse** and the **vkBasalt contributors** created the Vulkan post-processing layer that MAKO bundles through its maintained fork. Selected shader effects come from CeeJayDK/SweetFX and crosire/reshade-shaders; exact source and license details are in Third-party notices. MAKO also thanks the **Lossless Scaling developers** for the LS1 and LSFG models accessed through each user's licensed installation, the **Wine/vkd3d developers** whose shader translator enables the Vulkan LS1 path, and the **Decky Loader team**, community contributors, testers, guide authors, and creators who helped make the project possible. The open MAKO Scaler is independently implemented in this repository. The original copyright and license notices are preserved in LICENSE.md. MAKO is an independent community project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Lossless Scaling, Decky Loader, or the credited upstream projects. ## License MAKO is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later. Required upstream notices and the user-supplied proprietary-component boundary are recorded in Third-party notices, and visual sources are recorded in Asset provenance. Contributions are accepted under the policy in CONTRIBUTING.md. ## AI-assisted development MAKO uses coding agents as part of an evidence-driven engineering workflow while keeping architecture, review, validation, and release decisions under human ownership. See AI use in MAKO for the full approach. ## Contributors MAKO thanks everyone whose commits or co-authored work is in this repository. This gallery is generated from human authors and co-authors in the current branch's Git history; upstream projects and other forms of help are credited above. See Contributing to get involved.

# Agent2API **An AI routing gateway with Agent client takeover, unifying model APIs and local client configuration** **English** | [简体中文](./docs/README.zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](./docs/README.zh-Hant.md) | [日本語](./docs/README.ja.md) | [한국어](./docs/README.ko.md) | [Português (BR)](./docs/README.pt-BR.md) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-green)](./LICENSE) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/aimod-cc/Agent2API?include_prereleases)](https://github.com/aimod-cc/Agent2API/releases/latest) [![docker pulls](https://img.shields.io/docker/pulls/aimodcc/agent2api)](https://hub.docker.com/r/aimodcc/agent2api) [![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/aimod-cc/Agent2API?style=flat&color=yellow)](https://github.com/aimod-cc/Agent2API/stargazers) [![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20Docker-blue)](https://github.com/aimod-cc/Agent2API/releases/latest) [✨ Key Features](#-key-features) • [💬 Community & Support](#-community--support) • [🚀 Quick Start](#-quick-start) • [📦 Installation & deployment](./docs/install.en.md) • [📸 Screenshots](#-screenshots) • [🔧 Development & Build](#-development--build) • [📜 Usage Notice](#-usage-notice)
--- Agent2API is an **AI routing gateway with Agent client takeover**. It exposes a unified model API for custom AI providers and centralizes account routing, model mapping, gateway keys and request reports. It also manages local Agent clients' connection profiles, including importing, switching and previewing configuration changes. ## ✨ Key Features - 🔌 **Unified model APIs** — OpenAI Chat / Responses / Images and Anthropic Messages, with a unified model catalog; Raccoon, Loomy, Antigravity, ModelScope, WorkBuddy and Doubao Work supply image generation, while Raccoon, Loomy, Antigravity, ModelScope and WorkBuddy also support reference-image editing. Both are available as AI assistant tools - 🧭 **AI routing** — model mapping, account priority, load balancing, session affinity and failover in one place - 🤖 **Agent client takeover** — manage multiple connection profiles for local clients, import existing settings, preview writes and switch between the gateway and custom services - 🧩 **Plugin extensions** — additional provider implementations are installed and updated separately, not bundled with the application; custom providers do not require them - 🛡️ **Egress proxies** — select proxy-pool exits for accounts and update tasks - 🔑 **Gateway security** — scoped gateway keys, optional human verification for panel sign-in, and model requests refused by default until a key is configured - 📊 **Request reports** — request volume, success rate, token usage, cache hit rate and a 365-day heatmap - ⏰ **Background maintenance** — model catalog refresh, credential maintenance and software update checks; daily check-in runs per provider on that provider's own window (Qoder 10:01, ZCode 19:01, others follow the schedule time), plus a catch-up round that only touches accounts not yet checked in; additional provider-specific tasks are supplied by plugins - 🖥️ **Three deployment forms** — Windows / macOS / Linux desktop apps, headless Windows / Linux servers and Docker (amd64 / arm64); no Node runtime required, with a six-language interface ## ❤️ Sponsors
Thanks to ProxyLane for sponsoring this project! ProxyLane provides native static residential ISP proxies for AI accounts (Static Residential ISP): IPs come from real home broadband operators with low Scamalytics fraud scores, each IP is dedicated to you, with unlimited traffic, from $3.90. Add one exit per account on the Network proxy page. Use code AGENT2API25 for 25% off your first purchase.
## 💬 Community & Support - **QQ groups**: Agent2API chat groups — **group 1 (`1127656296`) and group 2 (`1130894674`) are almost full, please join group 3 (`1108276647`)**; search the number in QQ to join. - **Telegram group**: - **💖 Donate**: if Agent2API helps you, you are welcome to [buy the author a coffee](./docs/SPONSOR.md); donations are voluntary and unlock nothing. - **🤝 Sponsorship / business**: want to sponsor the project, or feature your product here? Email [541675139@qq.com](mailto:541675139@qq.com). ## 🚀 Quick start Three forms — pick the one that matches your setup; **the complete install, upgrade, uninstall and troubleshooting guide is in [Installation & deployment](./docs/install.en.md)**. | Form | Artifact | Interface | | --- | --- | --- | | **Desktop** (Windows / macOS / Linux) | `Agent2API__x64-setup.exe`, `_universal.dmg`, `_amd64.deb`, `_amd64.AppImage` | App window | | **Server** (Windows Server / Linux, headless) | `agent2api-server-windows-amd64.zip`, `agent2api-server-linux-.tar.gz` | Browser panel | | **Docker** | `aimodcc/agent2api:latest` (amd64 / arm64) | Browser panel | **Desktop**: add a custom provider and account, create a gateway key, then apply a connection profile on the Agent page or configure your client with `http://127.0.0.1:3065/v1` and that key. Additional provider capabilities require the corresponding plugin. **Server** (no GUI; registered as a system service and started at boot): ```bash # Linux tar -xzf agent2api-server-linux-amd64.tar.gz && cd agent2api-server-linux-amd64 && sudo bash install.sh ``` ```powershell # Windows Server (administrator PowerShell) Expand-Archive agent2api-server-windows-amd64.zip -DestinationPath C:\agent2api-pkg cd C:\agent2api-pkg; .\install-service.ps1 ``` **Docker**: ```bash docker run -d --name agent2api --restart unless-stopped -p 3065:3065 -v ./data:/data aimodcc/agent2api:latest ``` Whichever form you pick, open the panel afterwards (`http://127.0.0.1:3065/`; use the host IP for the server and Docker forms), register the admin account, then create a key on the "Gateway Keys" page. Connectivity check: `curl http://127.0.0.1:3065/health` **Mobile**: open `http://:3065/m` in a browser (you can "Add to Home Screen" for a full-screen PWA). For a standalone icon, install `Agent2API-.apk` (Android) or `Agent2API-.ipa` (iOS, unsigned — re-sign it yourself) from the Release. Details: [Install & deploy → Mobile](./docs/install.en.md#mobile). ## 📸 Screenshots ### Accounts ![Accounts page: global queue, per-model rate-limit cooldown, expiry and balance](./assets/screenshots/accounts.png) Add account: ![Add account: choose provider and edition, then sign in on the web](./assets/screenshots/add-account.png) ### Model management ![Model management: per-provider model catalog with rate, context and mappings](./assets/screenshots/models.png) ### Report Overview: requests / success rate / tokens / top model, with account and provider rankings, usage donuts and a 365-day activity heatmap: ![Report overview: stat cards, top accounts / providers, model and provider usage donuts](./assets/screenshots/report-overview.png) Trends: 24-hour **cache hit rate** (line) and **token consumption** (area) on twin axes, with a per-day token bar chart below: ![Report trends: dual-axis cache hit rate and token consumption, per-day token bars](./assets/screenshots/report-trends.png) ## 🔧 Development & Build ### Requirements - Rust >= 1.77 and the Tauri 2 toolchain (to compile the desktop app itself; Windows also needs the WebView2 runtime) - Node.js >= 18.17 (only to run `npm run tauri:*` and frontend build scripts; the desktop app does not depend on Node at runtime) - Target platforms: Windows / macOS / Linux desktops, headless Windows / Linux servers, and a Docker server ### Common scripts ```bash npm run tauri:install # Install desktop dependencies (same as npm --prefix desktop-tauri install) npm run tauri:dev # Launch the desktop app in dev mode (with hot reload) npm run tauri:build # Build the desktop installer npm run build:icon # Generate the icon source image (run after changing the icon design, then run tauri icon) ``` The build artifact is `target/release/bundle/nsis/Agent2API__x64-setup.exe` (about 8.6 MB as of 3.0; `src-tauri/.cargo/config.toml` points cargo's `target-dir` at the project root's `target/`). The macOS `.dmg` **can only be built on macOS** (`npm --prefix desktop-tauri run build -- --target universal-apple-darwin`) — it cannot be cross-compiled from Windows, so the official artifact comes from the CI `build` workflow (`macos-latest`, two targets merged). Docker images and the server archives used for in-container updates come from the same workflow's `linux-server` job, which reuses the Dockerfile's compile path so the executable inside is built from the same toolchain as the image. ## 📜 Usage Notice ### Credential and data security Account credentials are encrypted in the local database, but exports, backups and key files may still contain sensitive data. Keep them private; do not upload them to public repositories or cloud storage, or share them with others. ### No warranty The project is provided "as is", without guarantees of availability, stability, security or suitability for a particular purpose. Trademarks and services belong to their respective owners. The complete license and warranty terms are in [LICENSE](./LICENSE). ## 📄 License This project uses the same [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0)](./LICENSE) as the provider plugin repository. Use, modification and distribution, including commercial use, are permitted under the license. Preserve copyright and license notices and fulfill applicable source-code obligations. If you offer a modified version over a network, you must offer its Corresponding Source to those users. ## ⭐ Star History
**[Download the latest release](https://github.com/aimod-cc/Agent2API/releases/latest)** • **[Report an issue](https://github.com/aimod-cc/Agent2API/issues)** If this project helps you, a ⭐️ Star is appreciated!
